title.zh: 卷三百七十二 列傳第一百三十一 朱倬 王綸 尹穡 王之望 徐俯 沈與求 翟汝文 王庶 辛炳
title.en: Volume 372 Biographies 131: Zhu Zhuo, Wang Lun, Yin Se, Wang Zhiwang, Xu Fu, Shen Yuqiu, Di Ruwen, Wang Shu, Xin Bing
title.raw: 卷三百七十二 列傳第一百三十一 朱倬 王綸 尹穡 王之望 徐俯 沈與求 翟汝文 王庶 辛炳 Volume 372 Biographies 131: Zhu Zhuo, Wang Lun, Yin Se, Wang Zhiwang, Xu Fu, Shen Yuqiu, Di Ruwen, Wang Shu, Xin Bing

sentences.zh: 朱倬 王綸 尹穡 王之望 徐俯 沈與求 翟汝文 王庶 辛炳

translations.literal: Zhu Zhuo, Wang Lun, Yin Se, Wang Zhiwang, Xu Fu, Shen Yuqiu, Di Ruwen, Wang Shu, Xin Bing
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Zhuo, Wang Lun, Yin Se, Wang Zhiwang, Xu Fu, Shen Yuqiu, Di Ruwen, Wang Shu, and Xin Bing

sentences.zh: 朱倬，字漢章，唐宰相敬則之後，七世祖避地閩中，為閩縣人。

translations.literal: Zhu Zhuo, courtesy name Hanzhang, was a descendant of the Tang chancellor Jing Ze; his seventh-generation ancestor fled to Minzhong and became a resident of Min County.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Zhuo, whose courtesy name was Hanzhang, was descended from the Tang chancellor Jing Ze; seven generations earlier his family had fled into Fujian and settled in Min County.

sentences.zh: 世學《易》，入太學。

translations.literal: His family for generations studied the Book of Changes; he entered the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: The family had studied the Book of Changes for generations, and he enrolled in the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 宣和五年，登進士第，調常州宜興簿。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Xuanhe he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed assistant magistrate of Yixing in Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of the Xuanhe reign he passed the jinshi examination and was posted as assistant magistrate of Yixing in Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 金將犯邊，居民求避地，倬為具舟給食，眾賴以濟。

translations.literal: When Jin forces were about to invade the border, residents sought places of refuge; Zhuo provided boats and food, and the multitude relied on him to cross safely.
translations.idiomatic: As the Jin were about to strike the frontier, local people sought refuge elsewhere; Zhuo arranged boats and provisions for them, and many owed their escape to him.

sentences.zh: 未幾，民告澇於郡，郡檄倬考實，乃除田租什九，守怒，不能奪。

translations.literal: Before long the people reported flooding to the prefecture; the prefecture ordered Zhuo to verify it, and he then remitted nine-tenths of the field tax; the prefect was furious but could not overturn it.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward the people petitioned the prefecture about flood damage; the prefecture commissioned Zhuo to investigate, and he cut field rents by nine-tenths. The prefect was furious but could not reverse his decision.

sentences.zh: 張浚薦倬，召對，除福建、廣東西財用所屬官。

translations.literal: Zhang Jun recommended Zhuo; he was summoned for audience and appointed an official attached to the Fujian and Guangdong West fiscal agency.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun recommended him; summoned to an imperial audience, he was appointed to the Fujian and Guangdong West fiscal offices.

sentences.zh: 宣諭使明橐再薦于朝，時方以劉豫為憂，倬因賜對，策其必敗。

translations.literal: The imperial envoy Ming Nang recommended him again at court; the court was then worried about Liu Yu, and Zhuo, granted audience, predicted he would certainly be defeated.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial envoy Ming Nang recommended him to court again. With Liu Yu then a cause of alarm, Zhuo was granted an audience and predicted his certain downfall.

sentences.zh: 高宗大喜，詔改合入官。

translations.literal: Gaozong was greatly pleased and ordered his rank changed to he-ru.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozong was delighted and ordered his rank advanced to he-ru status.

sentences.zh: 與丞相秦檜忤，出教授越州。

translations.literal: He clashed with Chancellor Qin Hui and was sent out as instructor in Yuezhou.
translations.idiomatic: He fell out with Chancellor Qin Hui and was sent out to serve as an instructor in Yuezhou.

sentences.zh: 用張守薦，除諸王府教授。

translations.literal: On Zhang Shou's recommendation he was appointed instructor at the various imperial princes' establishments.
translations.idiomatic: On Zhang Shou's recommendation he was appointed instructor to the various imperial princes' households.

sentences.zh: 檜惡言兵，倬論掩骼事，又忤之。

translations.literal: Hui detested talk of war; Zhuo spoke on gathering exposed bones, and again offended him.
translations.idiomatic: Hui hated discussion of military affairs; when Zhuo spoke about collecting the unburied dead on the battlefield, he offended him once more.

sentences.zh: 梁汝嘉制置浙東，表攝參謀。

translations.literal: When Liang Rujia was commissioner for the Eastern Zhe circuit, he submitted a memorial appointing Zhuo acting staff adviser.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang Rujia was made commissioner for the Eastern Zhe circuit, he recommended Zhuo as acting staff adviser.

sentences.zh: 有群寇就擒，屬倬鞫問，獨竄二人，餘釋不問。

translations.literal: When a band of bandits had been captured, he was put in charge of interrogation; he alone had two flee, and the rest he released without inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: A band of brigands was taken; interrogation was entrusted to Zhuo. He let only two escape while releasing the rest without further questioning.

sentences.zh: 曰：“吾大父尉崇安日，獲寇二百，坐死者七十餘人。

translations.literal: He said: "When my grandfather served as magistrate of Chong'an, he seized two hundred bandits, of whom more than seventy were sentenced to death."
translations.idiomatic: He said, "When my grandfather was magistrate of Chong'an, he seized two hundred bandits, and more than seventy were put to death."

sentences.zh: 大父謂此饑民剽食爾，烏可盡繩以法？

translations.literal: My grandfather said these were hungry people plundering for food—how could one bind every one of them with the law?
translations.idiomatic: My grandfather said they were starving people looting for food—how could one apply the full weight of the law to them all?

sentences.zh: 悉除其罪，不以徼賞。

translations.literal: He wholly absolved their crimes and did not use this to seek reward.
translations.idiomatic: He cleared them all of guilt and did not seek reward for doing so.

sentences.zh: 吾其可愧大父乎？

translations.literal: How could I be unworthy before my grandfather?
translations.idiomatic: How could I shame my grandfather by acting otherwise?

sentences.zh: ”通判南劍。

translations.literal: He was appointed vice-prefect of Nanjian.
translations.idiomatic: He was then appointed vice-prefect of Nanjian.

sentences.zh: 建寇阿魏眾數千，劍鄰於建，兵懦不可用，倬重賞募卒擒獲，境內迄平。

translations.literal: The Jian bandit A Wei had several thousand followers; Nanjian neighbored Jian, the troops were cowardly and unusable; Zhuo offered heavy rewards to recruit soldiers and capture them, and within the borders there was peace at last.
translations.idiomatic: A band from Jian led by A Wei numbered several thousand men. Because Nanjian bordered Jian, the local troops were too weak to act; Zhuo offered rich bounties to recruit men who captured the rebels, and the district was pacified.

sentences.zh: 除知惠州。

translations.literal: He was appointed prefect of Huizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed prefect of Huizhou.

sentences.zh: 陛辭，因言嘗策劉豫必敗，高宗記其言，問：“卿久淹何所？

translations.literal: At his farewell audience he spoke of having once predicted Liu Yu's certain defeat; Gaozong remembered his words and asked: "Where have you been held back so long?"
translations.idiomatic: When he took leave of the throne he mentioned his earlier prediction that Liu Yu would fall. Gaozong remembered and asked, "Where have you been held back all this time?"

sentences.zh: ”倬曰：“厄於檜。

translations.literal: Zhuo said: "Hindered by Hui."
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo answered, "Blocked by Hui."

sentences.zh: ”上愀然慰諭，目送之。

translations.literal: The Emperor looked grave and comforted him with words, seeing him off with his gaze.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's expression darkened; he comforted Zhuo with kind words and watched him depart.

sentences.zh: 旬日間，除國子監丞，尋除浙西提舉，且命自今在內除提舉官，今朝辭上殿，蓋為倬設也。

translations.literal: Within ten days he was appointed Vice Director of the Directorate of Education, soon thereafter made Intendant for Zhexi; moreover it was ordered that from henceforth intendants appointed from within the court must present themselves at audience that same morning—a regulation made for Zhuo's sake.
translations.idiomatic: Within ten days he was made Vice Director of the Directorate of Education, then Intendant for Western Zhe; the court also ruled that hereafter intendants appointed from the central government must attend morning audience on the day of appointment—arrangements tailored for Zhuo.

sentences.zh: 既對，上曰：“卿以朕親擢出為部使者，使咸知內外任均。

translations.literal: After the audience the Emperor said: "You are being personally elevated by Us to go out as a commissioner, so that all may know that duties inside and outside are equal."
translations.idiomatic: After the audience the emperor said, "I am personally elevating you to serve as a regional commissioner, so everyone will see that posts at court and in the provinces carry equal weight."

sentences.zh: ”又曰：“人不知卿，朕獨知卿。

translations.literal: He also said: "People do not know you; We alone know you."
translations.idiomatic: He added, "Others do not know you, but I alone do."

sentences.zh: ”除右正言，累遷中丞。

translations.literal: He was appointed Right Rectifier of Writings and was repeatedly promoted to Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Right Rectifier of Writings and eventually rose to Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 嘗言：“人主任以耳目，非報怨任氣之地，必上合天心。

translations.literal: He once said: "The ruler entrusts one as eyes and ears; it is not a place for repaying grudges or venting temper—one must conform above to Heaven's intent."
translations.idiomatic: He once said, "The ruler appoints censors as his eyes and ears; the post is not for settling scores or venting spite—one's words must accord with Heaven's will."

sentences.zh: ”每上疏輒夙興露告，若上帝鑒臨。

translations.literal: Whenever he submitted a memorial he would rise early and make an open vow, as if the High God were observing.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he drafted a memorial he rose before dawn and prayed aloud, as though Heaven itself were watching.

sentences.zh: 奏疏凡數十，如發倉廩，蠲米價，減私鹽，核軍食，率焚稿不傳。

translations.literal: His memorials altogether numbered several tens, such as opening granaries, remitting rice prices, reducing private salt, and auditing army provisions; as a rule he burned the drafts and did not circulate them.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted dozens of memorials—on opening granaries, lowering rice prices, curbing private salt, auditing army rations—and as a rule burned his drafts rather than keep copies.

sentences.zh: 知貢舉，遷參知政事。

translations.literal: As chief examiner for the examinations he was promoted to Vice Commissioner of the Secretariat-Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: After supervising the civil examinations he was promoted to Vice Commissioner of the Secretariat-Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 紹興三十一年，拜尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year of Shaoxing he was appointed Right Vice Director of the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-first year of the Shaoxing reign he was appointed Right Vice Director of the Ministry of Works—effectively chief minister.

sentences.zh: 金兵犯江，倬陳戰、備、應三策，且謂兵應者勝，上深然之。

translations.literal: When Jin troops invaded the Yangzi region, Zhuo set forth three policies—fight, prepare, and respond—and said that he who could respond to events would win; the Emperor deeply approved.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin crossed the Yangzi, Zhuo proposed three policies: active combat, defensive preparation, and flexible response. He argued that victory belonged to those who could adapt; the emperor strongly agreed.

sentences.zh: 又策敵三事：上焉者為耕築計，中焉者守備，下則妄意絕江，金必出下策。

translations.literal: He also strategized three courses for the enemy: the superior was the farming-fortification plan, the middle was defense and preparation, the lower was reckless crossing of the river; Jin would certainly choose the lower course.
translations.idiomatic: He also analyzed three possible enemy moves: the best for them was to consolidate by farming and building fortifications; next was steadfast defense; worst was a rash attempt to cross the river. Jin would surely take the lowest course.

sentences.zh: 果如所料。

translations.literal: It turned out just as he had predicted.
translations.idiomatic: Events unfolded exactly as he had foretold.

sentences.zh: 史浩、虞允文、王淮、陳俊卿、劉珙之進用，皆倬所薦也。

translations.literal: The advancement of Shi Hao, Yu Yunwen, Wang Huai, Chen Junqing, and Liu Qi—all were Zhuo's recommendations.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hao, Yu Yunwen, Wang Huai, Chen Junqing, and Liu Qi all rose through his recommendations.

sentences.zh: 高宗自建康回鑾，有內禪意。

translations.literal: When Gaozong returned in imperial progress from Jiankang, he had in mind abdication.
translations.idiomatic: After Gaozong returned to the capital from Jiankang, he contemplated abdicating the throne.

sentences.zh: 倬密奏曰：“靖康之事正以傳位太遽，盍姑徐之。

translations.literal: Zhuo submitted a secret memorial saying: "The Jingkang affair arose precisely because the succession was transferred too hastily—why not defer it somewhat?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo secretly memorialized, "The disaster at Jingkang came because the throne passed too hastily; why not proceed more slowly?"

sentences.zh: ”心不自安，屢求去。

translations.literal: His heart was not at ease; he repeatedly sought to leave office.
translations.idiomatic: Uneasy in his own mind, he repeatedly asked to resign.

sentences.zh: 詔以觀文殿學士提舉江州太平興國宮。

translations.literal: An edict appointed him Academician of the Hall for Cultivating Culture to oversee the Taiping Xingguo Palace in Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to take up the honorary post of Academician of the Hall for Cultivating Culture and oversee the Taiping Xingguo Palace in Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 孝宗即位，諫臣以為言，降資政殿學士。

translations.literal: When Xiaozong took the throne, remonstrating officials spoke up, and his rank was reduced to Academician of the Hall of Governance.
translations.idiomatic: After Xiaozong's accession, remonstrators raised the issue, and he was demoted to Academician of the Hall of Governance.

sentences.zh: 明年致仕，卒。

translations.literal: The next year he retired from office and died.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he retired and died.

sentences.zh: 復元職，恤典如宰相，贈特進。

translations.literal: His original rank was restored; funeral rites were those of a chancellor; he was posthumously granted Special Advancement.
translations.idiomatic: His former rank was restored; he received a chancellor's funeral honors and was posthumously granted the title of Special Advancement.

sentences.zh: 孫著，淳熙十四年登第，仕至吏部尚書。

translations.literal: His grandson Zhu Zhuo passed the examinations in the fourteenth year of Chunxi and rose to Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Zhu Zhuo passed the examinations in the fourteenth year of Chunxi and rose to Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 王綸，字德言，建康人。

translations.literal: Wang Lun, courtesy name Deyan, was a native of Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Lun, whose courtesy name was Deyan, came from Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 幼穎悟，十歲能屬文。

translations.literal: In youth he was quick-witted; at ten he could compose literary pieces.
translations.idiomatic: Brilliant as a boy, he could write essays by the age of ten.

sentences.zh: 登紹興五年進士第，授平江府昆山縣主簿，曆鎮江府、婺州、臨安府教授，權國子正。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Shaoxing he passed the jinshi examination, was appointed recorder of Kunshan County in Pingjiang Prefecture, and successively served as instructor in Zhenjiang, Wuzhou, and Lin'an prefectures, with acting title of Rectifier of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi in the fifth year of Shaoxing, became recorder of Kunshan in Pingjiang, and later taught in Zhenjiang, Wuzhou, and Lin'an before serving as acting Rectifier of the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 時初建太學，亡舊規，憑吏省記，吏緣為奸。

translations.literal: At that time the Imperial Academy had just been established; old regulations were lost; one relied on clerks' records, and clerks used this to practice fraud.
translations.idiomatic: The Imperial Academy had only recently been founded, its old rules were gone, and affairs rested on clerks' ledgers—which the clerks exploited for graft.

sentences.zh: 綸厘正之，其弊稍革。

translations.literal: Lun corrected this, and its abuses were somewhat reformed.
translations.idiomatic: Lun straightened the procedures, and the worst abuses were curbed.

sentences.zh: 遷敕令所刪定官、諸王宮大小學教授兼權兵部郎官。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Editor of Statutes at the Edict Office, instructor at the Great and Small Schools for the Imperial Princes, with acting appointment as Secretary in the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Editor of Statutes, instructor at the princes' Great and Small Schools, and acting Secretary in the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 言：“孔門弟子與後世諸儒有功斯文者，皆得從祀先聖，今辟庠序，修禮樂，宜以其式頒諸郡縣。

translations.literal: He said: "The disciples of Confucius' gate and later scholars who had merit for cultured learning should all be allowed to join sacrifice to the Sage; now that schools are opening and ritual music is being restored, this model should be issued to all prefectures and counties."
translations.idiomatic: He argued that Confucius's disciples and later scholars who had served civilization deserved accompanying sacrifice in the Sage's temple; with schools reopening and ritual music restored, that standard ought to be promulgated through every prefecture and county.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，以御史中丞魏師遜薦，為監察御史，與秦檜論事，忤其意，師遜遂劾綸，且言：“智識淺昧，不能知綸。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year, on the recommendation of Censor-in-Chief Wei Shixun, he was made Investigating Censor; debating affairs with Qin Hui, he ran counter to Hui's intent; Shixun then impeached Lun, and furthermore said: "My knowledge is shallow and dim; I could not know Lun."
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year Wei Shixun, then Censor-in-Chief, recommended him as Investigating Censor. When he disputed policy with Qin Hui and crossed him, Shixun impeached Lun, adding bluntly that his own judgment was too shallow to have recognized Lun's faults.

sentences.zh: ”由此罷去。

translations.literal: Because of this he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: He was removed from office as a result.

sentences.zh: 逾年，知興國軍。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was appointed prefect of Xingguo Army.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he was made prefect of Xingguo district.

sentences.zh: 檜死，召為起居舍人兼崇政殿說書，尋兼權禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: When Hui died he was recalled as Attendant of the Secretariat and Lecturer at the Chongzheng Hall, soon also acting Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: After Hui's death he was recalled as Attendant of the Secretariat, lecturer at the Chongzheng Hall, and soon acting Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，試中書舍人。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he passed the examination for Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year he passed the examination for Secretariat Drafter.

sentences.zh: 高宗躬親政事，收攬威柄，召諸賢於散地，詔命填委，多綸所草。

translations.literal: Gaozong personally handled government affairs and gathered back imperial authority, summoning worthies from humble posts; edicts and appointments poured forth, many of them drafted by Lun.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong took government into his own hands, reclaimed authority, and called gifted men back from obscurity; edicts flooded out, most of them in Lun's hand.

sentences.zh: 綸奏守臣裕民事，乞毋拘五條，從之。

translations.literal: Lun memorialized that frontier officials should enrich the people's livelihood and begged that they not be bound by five articles; the Emperor assented.
translations.idiomatic: Lun urged that local officials ease the people's burdens and asked that they not be constrained by five standard formulae; the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 兼侍講。

translations.literal: He was additionally appointed Court Lecturer.
translations.idiomatic: He was also made Court Lecturer.

sentences.zh: 上喜讀《春秋左氏傳》，綸進講，與上意合。

translations.literal: The Emperor delighted in reading the Zuo Commentary to the Spring and Autumn Annals; Lun lectured upon it, in accord with the Emperor's mind.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor loved the Zuo Commentary to the Spring and Autumn Annals; Lun's lectures matched his tastes.

sentences.zh: 嘗同講讀官薦興化軍鄭樵學行，召對命官，且給筆劄，錄其所著史。

translations.literal: Once together with the lecture officials he recommended Zheng Qiao of Xinghua Circuit for learning and conduct; he was summoned for audience, given office, and supplied with paper and brush to record his historical writings.
translations.idiomatic: With fellow lecturers he recommended Zheng Qiao of Xinghua for scholarship and integrity; the court summoned him, granted rank, and supplied paper and brushes to copy his historical works.

sentences.zh: 兼直學士院，遷工部侍郎，仍兼直院。

translations.literal: He was additionally appointed to the Academy of Scholastic Honours, promoted to Vice Minister of Works while retaining his academy post.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the Hanlin Academy as additional academician, then rose to Vice Minister of Works while keeping his academy duties.

sentences.zh: 撰《吳玠神道碑》，稱上旨，賜宸翰褒寵。

translations.literal: He composed the Spirit-Road Stele for Wu Jie, which accorded with the Emperor's intent; the Emperor bestowed his own brush and praise.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Wu Jie's spirit-road stele in a style the emperor approved, earning imperial calligraphy and praise.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，除同知樞密院事。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year he was appointed Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year he was made Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 金將渝盟，邊報遝至，宰相沈該未敢以聞。

translations.literal: The Jin general was about to break the alliance; border reports arrived in rapid succession; Chancellor Shen Gai did not dare report it.
translations.idiomatic: A Jin commander was preparing to break the treaty; urgent dispatches arrived from the frontier, yet Chancellor Shen Gai dared not inform the throne.

sentences.zh: 綸率參知政事陳康伯、同知樞密院事陳誠之共白其事，乞備禦。

translations.literal: Lun together with Vice Commissioner Chen Kangbo and Co-Vice Commissioner Chen Cheng reported the matter and begged for defense preparations.
translations.idiomatic: Lun, Vice Commissioner Chen Kangbo, and Co-Vice Commissioner Chen Cheng told the emperor together and pleaded for defensive preparations.

sentences.zh: 已而綸病肺暍，告請祠，上遣御醫診視，且賜白金五百兩。

translations.literal: Before long Lun fell ill with heatstroke of the lungs, requested a sacrificial or retirement post; the Emperor sent the imperial physician to examine him and moreover bestowed five hundred taels of white silver.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Lun fell ill with lung heat-stroke, requested leave, and the emperor sent the court physician with five hundred taels of silver.

sentences.zh: 二十九年六月，朝論欲遣大臣為泛使覘敵，且堅盟好。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the twenty-ninth year the court debated sending a grand minister as a general envoy to reconnoiter the enemy and at the same time cement the alliance.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the twenty-ninth year the court debated dispatching a senior minister as envoy to gauge the enemy while reaffirming peaceful relations.

sentences.zh: 綸請行，乃以為稱謝使，曹勳副之。

translations.literal: Lun asked to go and was therefore made Envoy of Gratitude, with Cao Xun as deputy.
translations.idiomatic: Lun volunteered and was appointed Envoy of Gratitude, with Cao Xun as deputy.

sentences.zh: 至金，館禮甚隆。

translations.literal: Arriving in Jin territory, the reception ceremonial was very grand.
translations.idiomatic: In Jin territory he was received with elaborate ceremony.

sentences.zh: 一日，急召使入，金主禦便殿，惟一執政在焉，連發數問，綸條對，金主不能屈。

translations.literal: One day he was urgently summoned into the presence; the Jin ruler held court in the informal hall with only one minister present; he asked several questions in succession; Lun answered item by item, and the Jin ruler could not refute him.
translations.idiomatic: One day he was summoned abruptly to the informal hall, where only one Jin minister attended. The ruler fired question after question; Lun answered each in order until the Jin ruler could not best him.

sentences.zh: 九月，還朝入見，言：“鄰國恭順和好，皆陛下威德所致。

translations.literal: In the ninth month he returned to court and was received in audience, saying: "The neighboring state is respectful and compliant in peace—all brought about by Your Majesty's august virtue."
translations.idiomatic: He returned in the ninth month and told the emperor, "Our neighbor's courtesy and peaceful bearing come entirely from Your Majesty's august virtue."

sentences.zh: ”宰臣湯思退等皆賀。

translations.literal: Chancellors such as Tang Situ and others all congratulated him.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Tang Situ and others congratulated him.

sentences.zh: 然當時金已謀犯江，特以善意紿綸爾。

translations.literal: Yet at that time Jin had already planned invasion of the Yangzi—it was only that they used good intentions to deceive Lun.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the Jin were already planning to cross the Yangzi; they had merely deceived Lun with shows of goodwill.

sentences.zh: 綸舊疾作，力丐外，除資政殿大學士知福州，上解所禦犀帶賜之。

translations.literal: Lun's old illness returned; he strenuously begged an outside post and was appointed Grand Academician of the Hall for Governance as prefect of Fuzhou; the Emperor removed from his own waist the rhinoceros-horn belt and gave it to him.
translations.idiomatic: Lun's chronic illness flared again; he begged a post outside the capital and was made Grand Academician of the Hall for Governance and prefect of Fuzhou, with the emperor's own rhinoceros-horn belt as a parting gift.

sentences.zh: 明年，知建康府兼行宮留守。

translations.literal: The next year he was appointed prefect of Jiankang while also serving as custodian of the traveling palace.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he became prefect of Jiankang and custodian of the mobile palace.

sentences.zh: 敵犯江，綸每以守禦利害驛聞，上多從之。

translations.literal: When the enemy invaded the Yangzi, Lun repeatedly reported defense advantages and disadvantages by relay; the Emperor for the most part followed him.
translations.idiomatic: When the enemy struck the Yangzi, Lun sent rapid reports on defensive measures, most of which the emperor adopted.

sentences.zh: 三十一年八月，卒。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the thirty-first year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the eighth month of the thirty-first year.

sentences.zh: 贈左光祿大夫，諡章敏。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, with posthumous title Zhangmin.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and the posthumous title Zhangmin.

sentences.zh: 無子，以兄綽之子為後。

translations.literal: Having no son, his brother Chuo's son was made his heir.
translations.idiomatic: Childless, he adopted his brother Wang Chuo's son as heir.

sentences.zh: 尹穡，字少稷。

translations.literal: Yin Se, courtesy name Shaoji.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Se, whose courtesy name was Shaoji.

sentences.zh: 建炎中興，自北歸南。

translations.literal: At the revival during Jianyan he returned from the north to the south.
translations.idiomatic: At the Jianyan restoration he came south from the north.

sentences.zh: 紹興三十二年，與陸遊同為樞密院編修官。

translations.literal: In the thirty-second year of Shaoxing he and Lu You together were editors at the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-second year of Shaoxing he and Lu You served together as editors at the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 權知院史浩、同知王祖舜薦其博學有文，召對稱旨，二人並賜進士出身。

translations.literal: Acting Commissioner Shi Hao and Co-Commissioner Wang Zushun recommended them for broad learning and literary skill; summoned for audience they pleased the Emperor, and both were granted jinshi standing.
translations.idiomatic: Acting Commissioner Shi Hao and Co-Commissioner Wang Zushun praised their erudition; both pleased the emperor at audience and were granted jinshi standing.

sentences.zh: 孝宗獎用西北之士，隆興元年，除穡監察御史，尋除右正言。

translations.literal: Xiaozong prized and employed men from the northwest; in the first year of Longxing he appointed Se Investigating Censor, soon thereafter Right Rectifier of Writings.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozong favored scholars from the northwest; in the first year of Longxing he made Se Investigating Censor, then Right Rectifier of Writings.

sentences.zh: 二年五月，除殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the second year he was appointed Palace Attendant Censor within the Hall.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the second year he became Palace Attendant Censor.

sentences.zh: 曆遷諫議大夫，未幾而罷。

translations.literal: He was successively promoted to Remonstrator and before long dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Remonstrator, but was soon dismissed.

sentences.zh: 初，符離師潰，湯思退復相，金帥移書索地，詔侍從台諫集議。

translations.literal: At first, after the rout at Fuli, Tang Situ became chancellor again; the Jin commander sent a letter demanding territory; an edict ordered attendants, remonstrators, and censors to assemble for deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: After the debacle at Fuli, Tang Situ returned as chancellor; the Jin commander demanded territory by letter, and the emperor ordered court advisers and censors to debate the response.

sentences.zh: 穡時為監察御史，以為國家事力未備，宜與敵和，惟增歲幣，勿棄四州，勿請陵寢，則和議可成。

translations.literal: Se was then Investigating Censor; he held that national strength was not yet prepared and one should make peace with the enemy, only increasing annual tribute, not abandoning the four prefectures, not requesting return of imperial tombs—then peace could be concluded.
translations.idiomatic: Se, then Investigating Censor, argued that the state still lacked strength and should treat with the enemy: raise the annual tribute, keep the four prefectures, and do not press for recovery of the imperial tombs—only then could peace hold.

sentences.zh: 既而盧仲賢出使，為金所脅，又將遣王之望，張浚極言其不可。

translations.literal: Before long Lu Zhongxian went on embassy and was coerced by Jin; they were again about to dispatch Wang Zhiwang; Zhang Jun strongly said this could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Lu Zhongxian's mission was bullied by the Jin; as Wang Zhiwang was about to be sent abroad, Zhang Jun protested fiercely.

sentences.zh: 穡為右正言，懼和議弗就，因劾浚跋扈，未幾罷政。

translations.literal: Se was Right Rectifier and feared the peace talks would not succeed; he therefore impeached Jun for overbearing conduct; before long Jun was removed from power.
translations.idiomatic: As Right Rectifier, Se feared the peace would fail; he impeached Jun for arrogance, and Jun was soon driven from office.

sentences.zh: 後將割四郡，再易國書，歲幣如所索之數，而敵分兵入寇。

translations.literal: Later they were about to cede the four prefectures, exchange state letters again, and pay the annual tribute at the demanded amount, while the enemy divided troops and invaded.
translations.idiomatic: Later the court prepared to surrender the four prefectures and rewrite the state letters at the tribute level demanded—even as Jin armies crossed the border.

sentences.zh: 上意中悔。

translations.literal: The Emperor's mind midway regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor began to regret the course.

sentences.zh: 穡為侍御史，乞置獄，取不肯撤備及棄地者劾其罪，牽引凡二十餘人。

translations.literal: Se as Attendant Censor begged to set up a prison, take those who refused to withdraw preparations and those who abandoned territory, impeach their crimes, and implicate altogether more than twenty persons.
translations.idiomatic: As Attendant Censor, Se demanded a special inquiry to punish everyone who resisted demilitarization or opposed ceding land—more than twenty officials in all.

sentences.zh: 時方以和為急，擢穡為諫議大夫。

translations.literal: At that time peace was urgently pursued; Se was promoted to Remonstrator.
translations.idiomatic: With peace the urgent priority, Se was promoted to Remonstrator.

sentences.zh: 敵勢浸張，遠近震動，都督、同都督相繼辭行。

translations.literal: The enemy's strength gradually grew; near and far were shaken; the Commander-in-Chief and Co-Commander-in-Chief resigned their posts in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Enemy strength grew; the realm was alarmed; supreme commanders resigned one after another.

sentences.zh: 上書者攻和議之失，且言：“穡專附大臣為鷹犬，如張浚忠誠為國，天下共知，穡不顧公議，妄肆詆誹；

translations.literal: Memorial writers attacked the errors of the peace plan, and moreover said: "Se exclusively attaches himself to great ministers as a hawk and hound; as for Zhang Jun's loyalty to the state, all under Heaven know it—Se disregards public opinion and recklessly slanders him;"
translations.idiomatic: Petitioners denounced the peace policy and charged that "Se serves powerful ministers as their hawk and hound. Zhang Jun's loyalty is known throughout the realm, yet Se ignores public opinion and slanders him recklessly."

sentences.zh: 凡大臣不悅者皆逐之，相與表裡，以成奸謀，皆可斬。

translations.literal: "All great ministers he dislikes he drives away; they collude inside and out to carry out treacherous designs—all deserve execution."
translations.idiomatic: "Every senior official he dislikes is driven out; they work hand in glove to enact treacherous plots—all deserve death."

sentences.zh: ”上雖怒言者，而一時主議之臣與穡，皆相繼廢黜。

translations.literal: The Emperor was angry at the memorial writers, but for the moment the ministers who championed the policy together with Se were all dismissed one after another.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was enraged by the petitioners, yet the ministers who had backed Se and the peace policy were soon dismissed one after another.

sentences.zh: 先是，胡銓力言主和非是，大臣不悅，命銓與穡分往浙東西措置海道。

translations.literal: Earlier, Hu Quan forcefully argued that pursuing peace was wrong; the great ministers were displeased and ordered Quan and Se to go separately to Eastern and Western Zhe to arrange the sea routes.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Hu Quan had fiercely opposed the peace policy, angering the chief ministers, who sent Quan and Se to organize coastal defenses in Eastern and Western Zhe respectively.

sentences.zh: 二人挈家以行，為言者所劾，遂皆罷，語在《陳康伯傳》。

translations.literal: The two took their families along; they were impeached by memorial writers and both dismissed—the account is in the Biography of Chen Kangbo.
translations.idiomatic: Both men took their families with them, were impeached by petitioners, and were dismissed; the full account appears in Chen Kangbo's biography.

sentences.zh: 王之望

translations.literal: Wang Zhiwang
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhiwang

sentences.zh: 王之望，字瞻叔，襄陽穀城人，後寓居台州。

translations.literal: Wang Zhiwang, courtesy name Zhanshu, was a native of Gucheng in Xiangyang, later residing in Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhiwang, whose courtesy name was Zhanshu, came from Gucheng in Xiangyang and later settled in Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 父綱，登元符進士第，至通判徽州而卒。

translations.literal: His father Gang passed the jinshi in the Yuanfu era and rose to vice-prefect of Huizhou, where he died.
translations.idiomatic: His father Wang Gang passed the jinshi in the Yuanfu reign and served as vice-prefect of Huizhou before his death.

sentences.zh: 之望初以蔭補，紹興八年，登進士第。

translations.literal: Zhiwang was first appointed by yin privilege; in the eighth year of Shaoxing he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiwang entered service through yin privilege and passed the jinshi examination in the eighth year of Shaoxing.

sentences.zh: 教授處州，入為太學錄，遷博士。

translations.literal: He served as instructor in Chuzhou, entered the Imperial Academy as Registrar, and was promoted to Erudite.
translations.idiomatic: He taught in Chuzhou, became Registrar of the Imperial Academy, and was promoted to Erudite.

sentences.zh: 久之，出知荊門軍，提舉湖南茶鹽，改潼川府路轉運判官，尋改成都府路計度轉運副使、提舉四川茶馬。

translations.literal: After a long interval he went out as prefect of Jingmen Army, was intendant for Hunan tea and salt, was changed to Transport Assessor for Tongchuan Circuit, and soon was made Deputy Transport Commissioner and Fiscal Commissioner for Chengdu Circuit with charge over Sichuan tea and horses.
translations.idiomatic: After some years he became prefect of Jingmen, intendant for Hunan tea and salt, then Transport Assessor for Tongchuan Circuit, and soon Deputy Transport Commissioner and fiscal commissioner for Chengdu with authority over Sichuan tea and horses.

sentences.zh: 朝臣薦其才，召赴行在，除太府少卿，總領四川財賦。

translations.literal: Court ministers recommended his talent; he was summoned to the traveling palace, appointed Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Treasury, and made overall supervisor of Sichuan revenues.
translations.idiomatic: The court recommended his ability; summoned to the mobile capital, he was made Vice Director of the Imperial Treasury and overall supervisor of Sichuan finances.

sentences.zh: 金人渝盟，軍書旁午，調度百出，之望區畫無遺事。

translations.literal: The Jin violated the alliance; military dispatches arrived in rapid profusion; requisitions came by the hundred—Zhiwang organized everything without omission.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin broke the treaty, dispatches and requisitions poured in by the hundreds, and Zhiwang handled every detail without lapse.

sentences.zh: 第括民質劑未稅者，搜抉隱匿，得錢為緡四百六十八萬，眾鹹怨之。

translations.literal: He ranked people's pledges not yet taxed, searched out concealed property, and obtained cash in the amount of 4.68 million strings of cash—all resented him.
translations.idiomatic: He inventoried untaxed pledges and hunted down hidden assets, raising 4.68 million strings of cash—and earned widespread resentment.

sentences.zh: 後升太府卿。

translations.literal: Later he was promoted to Director of the Imperial Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: He was later promoted to Director of the Imperial Treasury.

sentences.zh: 隆興初，右諫議大夫王大寶疏之望罪，除集英殿修撰、提舉江州太平興國宮。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Longxing, Right Remonstrator Wang Dabao memorialized Zhiwang's crimes; he was appointed Compiler at the Hall for Assembled Eminence and charged with the Taiping Xingguo Palace in Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Longxing, Right Remonstrator Wang Dabao denounced him; he was made Compiler at the Hall for Assembled Eminence and custodian of the Taiping Xingguo Palace in Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 未幾，權戶部侍郎、江淮都督府參贊軍事。

translations.literal: Before long, acting Vice Minister of Revenue and staff adviser on military affairs to the Jiang-Huai Commandery Headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he served as acting Vice Minister of Revenue and staff adviser to the Jiang-Huai command headquarters.

sentences.zh: 之望雅不欲戰，請朝，因奏：“人主論兵與臣下不同，惟奉承天意而已。

translations.literal: Zhiwang by nature did not wish to fight; he requested audience and memorialized: "When the sovereign discusses military affairs he differs from subjects—one need only comply with Heaven's intent."
translations.idiomatic: Zhiwang disliked war by temperament; at audience he argued that a ruler's view of military affairs differs from his subjects'—one need only follow Heaven's will.

sentences.zh: 竊觀天意，南北之形已成，未易相兼，我之不可絕淮而北，猶敵之不可越江而南也。

translations.literal: "Observing Heaven's intent, the north-south situation has already taken shape and is not easily united; we cannot cut off the Huai and go north, just as the enemy cannot cross the Yangzi and come south."
translations.idiomatic: "Heaven's pattern shows north and south already fixed and hard to unite: we cannot abandon the Huai and march north any more than they can cross the Yangzi and drive south."

sentences.zh: 移攻戰之力以自守，自守既固，然後隨機制變，擇利而應之。

translations.literal: "Shift the strength used for attack and war to self-defense; once self-defense is secure, then adapt to circumstances, choose advantage, and respond."
translations.idiomatic: "Turn offensive strength to defense; once defense is firm, adapt to events, seize advantage, and respond accordingly."

sentences.zh: ”有旨留中。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the memorial retained at court.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the memorial kept at court.

sentences.zh: 俄兼直學士院。

translations.literal: Soon he was additionally appointed to the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He soon entered the Hanlin Academy as well.

sentences.zh: 湯思退力主息兵，奏除之望吏部侍郎、通問使。

translations.literal: Tang Situ forcefully advocated ceasing military action and memorialized to appoint Zhiwang Vice Minister of Personnel and Envoy for Inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Situ, pressing for peace, had Zhiwang appointed Vice Minister of Personnel and envoy to negotiate with the Jin.

sentences.zh: 尋議先遣小使覘敵，召之望還。

translations.literal: Soon they debated first sending a minor envoy to reconnoiter the enemy; Zhiwang was recalled.
translations.idiomatic: The court then debated sending a lesser envoy to scout the enemy first, and Zhiwang was recalled.

sentences.zh: 之望首以守備不足恃為告，上亟罷都督府，以之望為淮西宣諭使，甫拜命，又擢右諫議大夫。

translations.literal: Zhiwang first reported that defensive preparations could not be relied upon; the Emperor urgently abolished the Commandery Headquarters and made Zhiwang imperial envoy for Western Huai; upon receiving appointment he was also promoted to Right Remonstrator.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiwang warned that defenses were unreliable; the emperor quickly abolished the command headquarters, named him imperial envoy for Western Huai, and on appointment promoted him to Right Remonstrator.

sentences.zh: 之望因上章極言廷臣執偏見為身謀，乞明詔在庭，平其心於議論之際。

translations.literal: Zhiwang therefore submitted a memorial vehemently stating that court ministers clung to partial views for personal gain and begged a clear edict to the court to level their hearts in debate.
translations.idiomatic: He then memorialized that ministers clung to partisan views for private ends and begged an edict requiring even hearts in debate.

sentences.zh: 時思退主和議，浚主恢復，之望言似善，實陰為思退地也。

translations.literal: At that time Situ championed peace and Jun championed recovery; Zhiwang's words seemed reasonable but in fact secretly made room for Situ.
translations.idiomatic: Situ backed peace while Zhang Jun urged recovery; Zhiwang sounded even-handed but secretly aided Situ.

sentences.zh: 既而視師江上。

translations.literal: Before long he went to inspect the army on the Yangzi.
translations.idiomatic: He soon went to inspect troops on the Yangzi.

sentences.zh: 金復犯邊，遂上和、戰二策，且言措置守禦之備，疏奏未達，拜參知政事。

translations.literal: Jin again invaded the border; he then submitted both peace and war policies to the throne, and moreover spoke of arrangements for defensive preparation; the memorial had not yet arrived when he was appointed Vice Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin invaded again he offered both peace and war plans and detailed defensive measures; before the memorial arrived he was made Vice Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 既入，俄兼同知樞密院事。

translations.literal: After entering office, soon he was additionally Co-Vice Commissioner of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: After taking office he was soon also Co-Vice Commissioner of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 敵兵交至，濠、楚守將或棄城遁，上命湯思退督江、淮師；

translations.literal: Enemy troops arrived in succession; defenders of Hao and Chu sometimes abandoned cities and fled; the Emperor ordered Tang Situ to command Jiang-Huai armies.
translations.idiomatic: As enemy columns advanced, garrisons at Hao and Chu sometimes fled; the emperor ordered Tang Situ to command Jiang-Huai forces.

sentences.zh: 未行，復令之望督視，改同都督。

translations.literal: Before he departed, Zhiwang was again ordered to supervise; his title was changed to Co-Commander-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Before Situ left, Zhiwang was ordered to supervise instead and made Co-Commander-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 力辭不行。

translations.literal: He strenuously declined and would not go.
translations.idiomatic: He refused strenuously and would not go.

sentences.zh: 會太學諸生上書，上怒，欲加罪，之望救解之。

translations.literal: When Imperial Academy students submitted a joint memorial, the Emperor was angry and wished to punish them; Zhiwang interceded and secured their release.
translations.idiomatic: When academy students submitted a joint petition the emperor wished to punish them; Zhiwang interceded and won their release.

sentences.zh: 遂以參知政事勞師江、淮。

translations.literal: He thereupon went as Vice Commissioner to encourage the armies on the Jiang and Huai.
translations.idiomatic: He then went as Vice Commissioner to encourage the Jiang-Huai armies.

sentences.zh: 之望有文藝幹略，當秦檜時，落落不合或謂其有守。

translations.literal: Zhiwang had literary talent and practical ability; under Qin Hui he stood apart and did not fit in—some said he possessed integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Talented and capable, he had kept his distance under Qin Hui—some called that integrity.

sentences.zh: 紹興末年，力附和議，與思退相表裡，專以割地啖敵為得計，地割而敵勢益張，之望迄以此廢焉。

translations.literal: In the late Shaoxing years he forcefully joined the peace faction, worked hand in glove with Situ, took ceding territory to feed the enemy as expedient policy; territory was ceded while enemy power grew all the more—and Zhiwang was finally dismissed on this account.
translations.idiomatic: In late Shaoxing he embraced peace with Situ, treating land grants to the enemy as wisdom; the more territory was ceded the stronger the foe grew—and Zhiwang was ruined by it.

sentences.zh: 徐俯，字師川，洪州分寧人。

translations.literal: Xu Fu, courtesy name Shichuan, was a native of Fenning in Hongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Fu, whose courtesy name was Shichuan, came from Fenning in Hongzhou.

sentences.zh: 以父禧死國事，授通直郎，累官至司門郎。

translations.literal: Because his father Xi died in service to the state, he was granted Gentlemen for Unfailing Fidelity and rose through offices to Director of the Gate of the Capital.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xu Xi died in state service, so Fu received the rank of Gentlemen for Unfailing Fidelity and rose to Director of the Gate of the Capital.

sentences.zh: 靖康中，張邦昌僭位，俯遂致仕。

translations.literal: During Jingkang, Zhang Bangchang usurped the throne; Fu then retired from office.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jingkang crisis Zhang Bangchang seized the throne, and Fu retired.

sentences.zh: 時工部侍郎何昌言與其弟昌辰避邦昌，皆改名。

translations.literal: At that time Vice Minister of Works He Changyan and his younger brother Changchen avoided Bangchang and both changed their names.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister He Changyan and his brother Changchen, shunning Bangchang, both changed their names.

sentences.zh: 俯買婢名昌奴，遇客至，即呼前驅使之。

translations.literal: Fu bought a maid and named her Changnu; when guests arrived he would call "forward!" to have her lead the way—a deliberate mockery.
translations.idiomatic: Fu bought a maid named Changnu and, when guests came, would call "Forward!"—a pointed mockery of the He brothers.

sentences.zh: 建炎初，落致仕，奉祠。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianyan he was stripped of retirement status and given a sacrificial stipend.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Jianyan his retirement was revoked and he received a sacrificial stipend.

sentences.zh: 內侍鄭諶識俯於江西，重其詩，薦于高宗。

translations.literal: Inner Attendant Zheng Chen knew Fu in Jiangxi and prized his poetry; he recommended him to Gaozong.
translations.idiomatic: The inner attendant Zheng Chen met Fu in Jiangxi, admired his poetry, and recommended him to Gaozong.

sentences.zh: 胡直孺在經筵，汪藻在翰苑，迭薦之，遂以俯為右諫議大夫。

translations.literal: Hu Zhiru was in the Classics Lectures, Wang Zao in the Hanlin—they recommended him in turn, and Fu was made Right Remonstrator.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Zhiru in the Classics Lectures and Wang Zao in the Hanlin recommended him in turn, and Fu became Right Remonstrator.

sentences.zh: 中書舍人程俱言：“俯以前任省郎遽除諫議，自元豐更制以來未之有。

translations.literal: Secretariat Drafter Cheng Ju said: "Fu, from his former post as provincial secretary, was abruptly made Remonstrator—since the Yuanfeng reforms there has been no such case."
translations.idiomatic: Secretariat Drafter Cheng Ju objected that Fu had leapt from a provincial secretaryship to Remonstrator—unheard of since the Yuanfeng reforms.

sentences.zh: 考之古今，非陽城、種放，則未嘗不循序而進，願姑以所應者命之。

translations.literal: "Examining antiquity and the present, unless one were Yang Cheng or Zhong Fang, none advanced without following the proper sequence; Your Majesty might first appoint him to the post for which he is qualified."
translations.idiomatic: "History shows that except for Yang Cheng or Zhong Fang, no one skipped the proper sequence; Your Majesty should first give him the rank he has earned."

sentences.zh: 昔元稹在長慶間，擢知制誥，真不忝矣。

translations.literal: "Formerly Yuan Zhen in the Changqing era was promoted to Drafting Edicts—truly not unworthy."
translations.idiomatic: "Yuan Zhen in the Changqing era was promoted to drafting edicts—and was not unworthy."

sentences.zh: 緣其為荊南判司，命從中出，召為省郎，便知制誥，遂喧朝論，時謂荊南監軍崔潭峻實引之。

translations.literal: "But because he was an assistant in Jingnan, an order issued from the center, he was summoned as provincial secretary and at once knew drafting edicts, causing an uproar in court discussion; at the time they said the Jingnan supervising army Cui Tanjun had actually introduced him."
translations.idiomatic: "Yet he had been a Jingnan aide; a central order summoned him straight to the Secretariat and at once to drafting edicts, scandalizing the court—rumor said the Jingnan supervising officer Cui Tanjun had pushed him."

sentences.zh: 近亦傳俯與宦寺倡酬，稱其警策，恐或者不知陛下得俯之由。

translations.literal: "Recently it is also rumored that Fu exchanges verses with eunuchs, praising their wit—perhaps some do not know by what means Your Majesty obtained Fu."
translations.idiomatic: "Now Fu is said to exchange poems with eunuchs and praise their wit—perhaps not everyone knows how Your Majesty came to favor him."

sentences.zh: ”不報，俱遂罷。

translations.literal: No reply; Ju was thereupon dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not respond, and Ju was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 紹興二年，賜進士出身，兼侍讀。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shaoxing he was granted jinshi standing and additionally made Court Lecturer.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Shaoxing he was granted jinshi standing and made Court Lecturer.

sentences.zh: 三年，遷翰林學士，俄擢端明殿學士、簽書樞密院事。

translations.literal: In the third year he was promoted to Hanlin Academician, soon promoted to Academician of the Hall of Enlightened Governance and Coordinator of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he rose to Hanlin Academician, then Academician of the Hall of Enlightened Governance and Coordinator of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 四年，兼權參知政事。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he additionally served as acting Vice Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he also served as acting Vice Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 宰相朱勝非言：“襄陽上流，所當先取。

translations.literal: Chancellor Zhu Shengfei said: "Xiangyang lies on the upper Yangzi and ought to be taken first."
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Zhu Shengfei said, "Xiangyang on the upper Yangzi should be taken first."

sentences.zh: ”帝曰：“盍就委岳飛？

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Why not entrust this to Yue Fei?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked, "Why not entrust it to Yue Fei?"

sentences.zh: ”參政趙鼎曰：“知上流利害，無如飛者。

translations.literal: Vice Commissioner Zhao Ding said: "No one knows the currents and hazards on the river like Fei."
translations.idiomatic: Vice Commissioner Zhao Ding replied, "No one knows the river's currents and hazards like Fei."

sentences.zh: ”俯獨持不可，帝不聽。

translations.literal: Fu alone maintained it could not be done; the Emperor did not heed him.
translations.idiomatic: Fu alone objected; the emperor ignored him.

sentences.zh: 會劉光世乞入奏，鼎言：“方議出師，大將不宜離軍。

translations.literal: When Liu Guangshi requested to come to court for audience, Ding said: "Just as we are debating sending troops, a great general ought not leave his army."
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Guangshi asked to attend court, Ding said, "With a campaign under debate, a field commander must not leave his army."

sentences.zh: ”俯欲許之，鼎固爭，俯乃求去，提舉洞霄宮。

translations.literal: Fu wished to grant it; Ding argued firmly; Fu then asked to leave and was made custodian of the Dongxiao Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Fu wanted to allow it; Ding argued hard; Fu then resigned and was made custodian of the Dongxiao Palace.

sentences.zh: 九年，知信州。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was appointed prefect of Xinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he became prefect of Xinzhou.

sentences.zh: 中丞王次翁論其不理郡事，予祠。

translations.literal: Censor Wang Ciweng accused him of neglecting prefectural duties; he was given a stipend post.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Wang Ciweng charged him with neglecting the prefecture, and he was given a stipend post.

sentences.zh: 明年，卒。

translations.literal: The next year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died the following year.

sentences.zh: 俯才俊，與曾幾、呂本中游，有詩集六卷。

translations.literal: Fu was talented; he associated with Zeng Ji and Lü Benzhong and left a collection of poetry in six fascicles.
translations.idiomatic: A gifted poet, he moved in the circle of Zeng Ji and Lü Benzhong and left a six-fascicle collection.

sentences.zh: 沈與求

translations.literal: Shen Yuqiu
translations.idiomatic: Shen Yuqiu

sentences.zh: 沈與求，字必先，湖州德清人。

translations.literal: Shen Yuqiu, courtesy name Bixian, was a native of Deqing in Huzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Yuqiu, whose courtesy name was Bixian, came from Deqing in Huzhou.

sentences.zh: 登政和五年進士第，累遷至明州通判。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi in the fifth year of Zhenghe and was repeatedly promoted to vice-prefect of Mingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi in the fifth year of Zhenghe and rose to vice-prefect of Mingzhou.

sentences.zh: 以御史張守薦，召對，除監察御史。

translations.literal: On Investigating Censor Zhang Shou's recommendation he was summoned for audience and appointed Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shou recommended him; summoned to audience, he became Investigating Censor.

sentences.zh: 上疏論執政，遷兵部員外郎，自劾以為言苟不當，不應得遷。

translations.literal: He memorialized criticizing those in power and was promoted to Secretary in the Ministry of War; he impeached himself holding that if his words were not right he ought not be promoted.
translations.idiomatic: He criticized those in power and was promoted to Secretary in the Ministry of War, then impeached himself on the ground that wrong counsel should not be rewarded.

sentences.zh: 上乃行其言，除殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: The Emperor then carried out his proposals and appointed him Palace Attendant Censor within the Hall.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor adopted his advice and made him Palace Attendant Censor.

sentences.zh: 上在會稽，或勸幸饒、信，有急則入閩。

translations.literal: When the Emperor was at Kuaiji, some urged traveling to Rao and Xin, with the option of entering Min in an emergency.
translations.idiomatic: While the court was at Kuaiji, some urged retreat to Rao and Xin, with Fujian as a last refuge.

sentences.zh: 與求以為今日根本正在江、浙，宜進都建康，以圖恢復。

translations.literal: Yuqiu held that today's foundation lies in Jiang and Zhe; one ought to advance and make Jiankang the capital to plan recovery.
translations.idiomatic: Yuqiu argued that the realm's foundation lay in Jiang and Zhe and that the court should advance to Jiankang to plan recovery.

sentences.zh: 論范宗尹年少為相，恐誤國事。

translations.literal: He criticized Fan Zongyin for being young as chancellor and likely to harm state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He warned that Fan Zongyin was too young as chancellor and would harm state affairs.

sentences.zh: 上不悅，以直龍圖閣知台州。

translations.literal: The Emperor was displeased and appointed him to the Direct Palace with dragon-designation as prefect of Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Displeased, the emperor sent him out as prefect of Taizhou with the title Direct Palace.

sentences.zh: 宗尹罷，召還，再除侍御史。

translations.literal: When Zongyin was dismissed he was recalled and again appointed Attendant Censor.
translations.idiomatic: When Zongyin fell he was recalled as Attendant Censor.

sentences.zh: 時軍儲窘乏，措置諸鎮屯田，與求取古今屯田利害，為《集議》二卷上之，詔付戶部看詳。

translations.literal: At that time army provisions were straitened; colonies were established at the various garrisons; Yuqiu collected the benefits and harms of farming colonies through the ages and submitted a Collected Deliberations in two fascicles; an edict ordered the Ministry of Revenue to examine it.
translations.idiomatic: With army stores low, garrison colonies were debated; Yuqiu compiled ancient and modern precedents on military farming in two fascicles and sent them to the Ministry of Revenue for review.

sentences.zh: 江西安撫、知江州朱勝非未至，而馬進寇江州陷之，與求論九江之陷，由勝非赴鎮太緩，勝非罷去。

translations.literal: Jiangxi Pacification Commissioner and Jiangzhou prefect Zhu Shengfei had not yet arrived when Ma Jin attacked Jiangzhou and took it; Yuqiu argued that the fall of Jiujiang was because Shengfei went to his post too slowly; Shengfei was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangxi commissioner Zhu Shengfei had not reached Jiangzhou when Ma Jin seized it; Yuqiu blamed the loss of Jiujiang on Shengfei's delay, and Shengfei was removed.

sentences.zh: 時方多事，百司稽違，與求援元豐舊制，請許台諫官彈奏，上從之。

translations.literal: At that time affairs were many; all offices dragged their feet; Yuqiu cited the Yuanfeng old system and begged that investigating and remonstrating officials be allowed to impeach; the Emperor assented.
translations.idiomatic: With affairs pressing and offices stalling, Yuqiu cited Yuanfeng rules allowing censors to impeach, and the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 與求再居言路，或疑凡范宗尹所引用者，將悉論出之。

translations.literal: When Yuqiu again held the remonstrating post, some suspected that everyone Fan Zongyin had employed would be driven out.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned to the remonstrating post, some feared he would purge everyone Zongyin had appointed.

sentences.zh: 與求曰：“ 近世朋黨成風，人才不問賢否，皆視宰相出處為進退。

translations.literal: Yuqiu said: "In recent times factionalism has become the custom; talent, whether worthy or not, all look to whether the chancellor brought one in for advancement or dismissal."
translations.idiomatic: Yuqiu said, "Faction has become habit: men rise or fall according to which chancellor brought them in, not whether they are fit."

sentences.zh: 今當別人才邪正而言之，豈可謂一時所用皆不賢哉？

translations.literal: "Today one ought to distinguish talent as honest or corrupt in speaking of them—how can one say that everyone employed at one time is unworthy?"
translations.idiomatic: "We should judge men by honesty and corruption—not declare an entire administration unworthy."

sentences.zh: ”人服其言。

translations.literal: People were convinced by his words.
translations.idiomatic: His argument carried the day.

sentences.zh: 呂頤浩再相，禦營統制辛永宗、樞密富直柔、右司諫韓璜屢言其短。

translations.literal: Lü Yihao became chancellor again; Commander of the Imperial Guard Forces Xin Yongzong, Military Affairs Commissioner Fu Zhirou, and Right Remonstrator Han Huang repeatedly spoke of his faults.
translations.idiomatic: When Lü Yihao returned as chancellor, Guard Commander Xin Yongzong, Military Affairs Commissioner Fu Zhirou, and Remonstrator Han Huang repeatedly attacked him.

sentences.zh: 與求劾直柔附會永宗兄弟，為致身之資。

translations.literal: Yuqiu impeached Zhirou for toadying to the Yongzong brothers as a means of personal advancement.
translations.idiomatic: Yuqiu impeached Zhirou for currying favor with the Yongzong brothers to advance himself.

sentences.zh: 上遂出永宗，而璜、直柔亦相繼罷黜。

translations.literal: The Emperor thereupon removed Yongzong, while Huang and Zhirou were also dismissed in succession.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor removed Yongzong; Huang and Zhirou were dismissed soon after.

sentences.zh: 遷御史中丞。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 時禁衛寡弱，諸將各擁重兵，與求言：“漢有南北軍，唐用府兵，彼此相維，使無偏重之勢。

translations.literal: At that time the palace guard was few and weak and each general held heavy troops; Yuqiu said: "Han had Northern and Southern Armies; Tang used militia from fubing—each checked the other so there was no tendency toward overweighted power."
translations.idiomatic: With the palace guard weak and generals holding private armies, Yuqiu cited Han's Northern and Southern Armies and Tang's fubing militia as mutual checks against concentrated force.

sentences.zh: 今兵權不在朝廷，雖有樞密院及三省兵房、尚書兵部，但行文字而已。

translations.literal: "Today military authority is not in the court; although there is the Bureau of Military Affairs and the three departments' military office and the Ministry of War in the Department of State Affairs, they only circulate documents."
translations.idiomatic: "Today real military power is not at court: the Bureau of Military Affairs, the three departments' military office, and the Ministry of War merely shuffle papers."

sentences.zh: 願詔大臣益修兵政，助成中興之勢。

translations.literal: "May Your Majesty order great ministers to further repair military government and help achieve the momentum of restoration."
translations.idiomatic: "Let great ministers restore military governance and build momentum for restoration."

sentences.zh: ”浙西安撫劉光世來朝，以繒帛、方物為獻，上已分乞六宮，與求奏：“今為何時而有此。

translations.literal: Zhexi Pacification Commissioner Liu Guangshi came to court and presented silks and local products as gifts; the Emperor had already distributed them among the six palaces; Yuqiu memorialized: "What time is this, yet there is this?"
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Guangshi of Zhexi brought silks and local gifts—the emperor had already divided them among the palaces—Yuqiu asked, "What season is this for such presents?"

sentences.zh: ”時已暮，疏入，上命追取斥還。

translations.literal: It was already evening; when the memorial entered, the Emperor ordered them chased down and returned.
translations.idiomatic: It was evening; the memorial arrived and the emperor ordered the gifts seized and sent back.

sentences.zh: 內侍馮益請別置禦馬院，自領其事，又擅穿皇城便門。

translations.literal: Inner Attendant Feng Yi requested a separate imperial horse park and personally to oversee it; he also on his own authority opened a secret gate in the imperial city wall.
translations.idiomatic: Inner attendant Feng Yi sought a private imperial stud and opened a secret gate in the palace wall on his own authority.

sentences.zh: 與求劾益專恣，請治其罪。

translations.literal: Yuqiu impeached Yi for arrogant license and begged punishment according to law.
translations.idiomatic: Yuqiu impeached him for arrogance and demanded legal punishment.

sentences.zh: 諜報劉豫在淮陽造舟，議者多欲于明州向頭設備。

translations.literal: Spies reported Liu Yu was building boats at Huaiyang; many in debate wished to prepare defenses at Xiangtou in Mingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Spies reported Liu Yu building boats at Huaiyang; many wanted defenses at Xiangtou in Mingzhou.

sentences.zh: 與求言：“使賊舟至此，則入吾腹心之地。

translations.literal: Yuqiu said: "If enemy boats reach this place, they will enter the heart of our territory."
translations.idiomatic: Yuqiu warned, "If enemy ships reach Xiangtou, they will be deep inside our territory."

sentences.zh: 臣聞海舟自京東入浙，必由泰州石港、通州料角崇明鎮等處，次至平江南北洋，次至秀州金山，次至向頭。

translations.literal: "I hear that sea boats entering Zhe from Jingdong must pass Shigang in Taizhou, Liaojiao in Tongzhou, Chongming town, and the like; next the north shore south of Pingjiang; next Jinshan in Xiuzhou; next Xiangtou."
translations.idiomatic: "Sea routes from Jingdong into Zhe pass Shigang in Taizhou, Liaojiao in Tongzhou, Chongming, then Pingjiang's north shore, Jinshan in Xiuzhou, and finally Xiangtou."

sentences.zh: 又聞料角水勢湍險，必得沙上水手方能轉運。

translations.literal: "I also hear the water at Liaojiao is swift and treacherous—one must have sailors who know the sands to make the transit."
translations.idiomatic: "Liaojiao's currents are swift and treacherous—only sand pilots can navigate them."

sentences.zh: 宜於石港、料角等處拘收水手，優給錢糧而存養之，以備緩急。

translations.literal: "It is fitting at Shigang, Liaojiao, and the like to register sailors, give them generous pay and grain and keep them on hand for emergencies."
translations.idiomatic: "Register sailors at Shigang, Liaojiao, and similar points, pay them well, and keep them ready for emergencies."

sentences.zh: 兩浙轉運副使徐康國自溫州進發宣和間所制間金、銷金屏障什物，與求奏曰：“陛下儉侔大禹，今康國欲以微物累盛德，乞斥而焚之，仍顯黜康國。

translations.literal: Zhexi Deputy Transport Commissioner Xu Kangguo from Wenzhou presented gold-inlaid and gold-trimmed screen objects made in the Xuanhe era; Yuqiu memorialized: "Your Majesty is thrifty as Great Yu; now Kangguo wishes to burden Your lofty virtue with trifles—may Your Majesty reject and burn them and clearly demote Kangguo."
translations.idiomatic: Deputy Transport Commissioner Xu Kangguo brought Xuanhe-era gold-inlaid screens from Wenzhou; Yuqiu urged, "Your Majesty is thrifty as Yu the Great; these trifles insult that virtue—burn them and demote Kangguo."

sentences.zh: ”從之。

translations.literal: The Emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 與求曆御史三院，知無不言，前後幾四百奏，其言切直，自敵己已下有不能堪者。

translations.literal: Yuqiu served through all three censorial bureaus and spoke without holding back; his memorials altogether approached four hundred; his words were cutting and direct—from enemies down to partisans there were none who could bear them.
translations.idiomatic: Serving all three censorial bureaus, he spoke without restraint—nearly four hundred memorials, sharp and direct—so that foes and allies alike found him hard to bear.

sentences.zh: 上時有所訓敕，每曰：“汝不識沈中丞邪？

translations.literal: When the Emperor at times gave instructions, he would always say: "Do you not know Vice Censor Shen?"
translations.idiomatic: When giving instructions the emperor would say, "Do you not know Vice Censor Shen?"

sentences.zh: ”移吏部尚書兼權翰林學士兼侍讀，遂出為荊湖南路安撫使、知潭州。

translations.literal: He was moved to Minister of Personnel with acting appointment as Hanlin Academician and Court Lecturer, then went out as Pacification Commissioner for southern Hunan and prefect of Tanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Minister of Personnel, acting Hanlin academician and court lecturer, then sent out as Hunan pacification commissioner and prefect of Tanzhou.

sentences.zh: 引疾丐祠許之。

translations.literal: He cited illness and begged a sacrificial post; this was granted.
translations.idiomatic: He pleaded illness for a sacrificial post and was allowed to retire.

sentences.zh: 四年，出知鎮江府兼兩浙西路安撫使。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he went out as prefect of Zhenjiang while also serving as Pacification Commissioner for Western Zhe.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he became prefect of Zhenjiang and pacification commissioner for Western Zhe.

sentences.zh: 復以吏部尚書召，除參知政事。

translations.literal: Again summoned as Minister of Personnel, he was appointed Vice Commissioner of the Secretariat-Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled as Minister of Personnel, he was made Vice Commissioner of the Secretariat-Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 金人將入寇，上諭輔臣曰：“朕當親總六軍。

translations.literal: The Jin were about to invade; the Emperor instructed the chief ministers: "We shall personally command the Six Armies."
translations.idiomatic: With the Jin about to invade, the emperor told his ministers, "I shall personally lead the Six Armies."

sentences.zh: ”與求贊之曰：“今日親征，皆由聖斷。

translations.literal: Yuqiu endorsed it, saying: "Today's personal campaign is entirely by Your Majesty's sage decision."
translations.idiomatic: Yuqiu agreed: "This personal campaign rests entirely on Your Majesty's decision."

sentences.zh: ”上意決親征，書《車攻詩》以賜。

translations.literal: The Emperor resolved on a personal campaign and wrote out the poem "Chariots in Array" to bestow on him.
translations.idiomatic: Resolved on campaigning in person, the emperor copied out the "Chariots in Array" and gave it to him.

sentences.zh: 上曰：“朕以二聖在遠，屈己通和。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "With the Two Sovereigns far away, We humbled Ourselves to seek peace."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "With the two captive emperors still in the north, I humbled myself to seek peace."

sentences.zh: 今豫逆亂如此，安可復忍？

translations.literal: "Now Yu rebels and wreaks such disorder—how can We endure it further?"
translations.idiomatic: "Now that Yu's rebellion has come to this, how can I bear it any longer?"

sentences.zh: ”與求曰：“和親乃金人屢試之策，不足信也。

translations.literal: Yuqiu said: "Peace by marriage is a stratagem the Jin have tried again and again—it cannot be trusted."
translations.idiomatic: Yuqiu replied, "Marriage alliances are a trick the Jin have used repeatedly—they are not to be trusted."

sentences.zh: ”因奏：“諸將分屯江岸，而敵人往來淮甸，當遣岳飛自上流取間道乘虛擊之，彼必有反顧之憂。

translations.literal: He therefore memorialized: "The various generals are posted along the Yangzi banks while the enemy comes and goes in the Huai region—Yue Fei ought to be sent from the upper reaches by a side road to strike where they are empty; they will surely have worries about their rear."
translations.idiomatic: He urged that while generals held the Yangzi line the enemy moved freely on the Huai—Yue Fei should strike from upstream by a side route and force them to look to their rear.

sentences.zh: ”上曰：“當如此措置。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "It should be arranged in this way."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "That is how it should be done."

sentences.zh: 五年，兼權知樞密院事。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he additionally served as acting Vice Commissioner of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he also served as acting Vice Commissioner of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 時張浚視師江上，以行府為名，言知泰州邵彪及具營田利害事，乞送尚書省。

translations.literal: At that time Zhang Jun was inspecting the army on the Yangzi under the title of field headquarters; he spoke of knowing Taizhou defender Shao Biao and the benefits and harms of military colonies, and begged that these be sent to the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun, commanding on the Yangzi as a field headquarters, reported on Shao Biao of Taizhou and colony farming and asked the Secretariat to review it.

sentences.zh: 有旨從之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered compliance.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 與求不能平，曰：“三省、樞密院乃奉行行府文書邪？

translations.literal: Yuqiu could not accept it and said: "Are the three departments and the Bureau of Military Affairs to execute documents for a field headquarters?"
translations.idiomatic: Yuqiu protested, "Are the three departments and Military Affairs Bureau merely clerks for a field headquarters?"

sentences.zh: ”六年，張浚復欲出視師，不告之同列。

translations.literal: In the sixth year Zhang Jun again wished to go out to inspect the army without informing his colleagues.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year Zhang Jun again planned to take the field without telling his colleagues.

sentences.zh: 及得旨，乃退而歎曰：“此大事也，吾不與聞，何以居位？

translations.literal: When he received the edict he withdrew and sighed: "This is a great affair—if I am not informed, how can I hold my post?"
translations.idiomatic: Receiving the order he withdrew and sighed, "This is a grave matter—how can I remain in office if I am not told?"

sentences.zh: ”遂丐祠，罷，出知明州。

translations.literal: He thereupon begged a sacrificial post, was dismissed, and went out as prefect of Mingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He begged a sacrificial post, resigned, and was sent out as prefect of Mingzhou.

sentences.zh: 七年，上在平江，召見，除同知樞密院事；

translations.literal: In the seventh year, when the Emperor was at Pingjiang, he was summoned and appointed Co-Vice Commissioner of Military Affairs;
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, while the emperor was at Pingjiang, he was summoned as Co-Vice Commissioner of Military Affairs;

sentences.zh: 從至建康，遷知樞密院事。

translations.literal: he followed to Jiankang and was promoted to Commissioner of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: he followed to Jiankang and was promoted to Commissioner of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 薨，贈左銀青光祿大夫，諡忠敏。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously granted Left Silver Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, posthumous title Zhongmin.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously granted Left Silver Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the posthumous title Zhongmin.

sentences.zh: 翟汝文

translations.literal: Di Ruwen
translations.idiomatic: Di Ruwen

sentences.zh: 翟汝文，字公巽，潤州丹陽人。

translations.literal: Di Ruwen, courtesy name Gongxun, was a native of Danyang in Runzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Di Ruwen, whose courtesy name was Gongxun, came from Danyang in Runzhou.

sentences.zh: 登進士第，以親老不調者十年。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination; because his parents were old he did not take office for ten years.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi but did not take office for ten years while caring for aged parents.

sentences.zh: 擢議禮局編修官，召對，徽宗嘉之，除秘書郎。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Compiler in the Board for Deliberating Ritual, summoned for audience; Huizong was pleased with him and appointed him Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to ritual compiler and summoned to audience, he pleased Huizong and was made Secretary.

sentences.zh: 三館士建議東封，汝文曰：“治道貴清淨。

translations.literal: Scholars of the Three Institutes proposed an eastern feng; Ruwen said: "The way of governance values purity and quiet."
translations.idiomatic: When Three Institutes scholars proposed an eastern feng, Ruwen said, "Good government values purity and restraint."

sentences.zh: 今不啟上述三代禮樂，而師秦、漢之侈心，非所願也。

translations.literal: "Now instead of reviving the ritual music of the Three Dynasties above, you take the extravagant heart of Qin and Han—this is not what I wish."
translations.idiomatic: "Rather than restoring the rites of the Three Dynasties, you copy Qin and Han extravagance—that is not what I desire."

sentences.zh: ”責監宿州稅。

translations.literal: He was punished by supervision of the Suzhou tax office.
translations.idiomatic: He was demoted to supervisor of the Suzhou tax office.

sentences.zh: 久之，召除著作郎，遷起居郎。

translations.literal: After a long interval he was summoned and appointed Compiler; he was promoted to Attendant of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was recalled as Compiler and promoted to Attendant of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 皇太子就傅，命汝文勸講，除中書舍人。

translations.literal: When the heir apparent received tutors, Ruwen was ordered to lecture and was appointed Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince received tutors, Ruwen lectured for him and was made Secretariat Drafter.

sentences.zh: 言者謂汝文從蘇軾、黃庭堅遊，不可當贊書之任，出知襄州，移知濟州，復知唐州，以謝章自辨罷。

translations.literal: Memorial writers said Ruwen had associated with Su Shi and Huang Tingjian and could not hold the post of drafting praise; he went out as prefect of Xiangzhou, was moved to Jizhou, again knew Tangzhou, and on a memorial of thanks argued in his own defense and was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Critics said he had traveled with Su Shi and Huang Tingjian and was unfit to draft imperial praise; he served as prefect of Xiang, Jizhou, and Tang, then resigned after self-defense in a thanks memorial.

sentences.zh: 未幾，起知陳州。

translations.literal: Before long he was raised to know Chenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed prefect of Chenzhou.

sentences.zh: 召拜中書舍人，外制典雅，一時稱之。

translations.literal: Recalled as Secretariat Drafter, his external compositions were elegant—at the time he was praised.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled as Secretariat Drafter, his edicts were elegant and widely praised.

sentences.zh: 命同修《哲宗國史》，遷給事中。

translations.literal: Ordered to compile jointly the National History of Zhezong, he was promoted to Supervising Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Ordered to compile the National History of Zhezong, he rose to Supervising Secretary.

sentences.zh: 高麗使入貢，詔班侍從之上，汝文言：“《春秋》之法，王人雖微，序諸侯上。

translations.literal: When a Goryeo envoy came to offer tribute, an edict ranked him above the attendant ministers; Ruwen said: "By the method of the Spring and Autumn Annals, a king's man, though humble, is ranked above feudal lords."
translations.idiomatic: When a Goryeo envoy arrived, an edict placed him above attendants; Ruwen cited the Spring and Autumn Annals: even a king's humble messenger ranks above feudal lords.

sentences.zh: 不可卑近列而尊陪臣。

translations.literal: "One cannot demean those of near rank and honor accompanying ministers."
translations.idiomatic: "He must not be set below nearby ministers while honored above them."

sentences.zh: ”上遂命如舊制。

translations.literal: The Emperor thereupon ordered it according to the old system.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor restored the old protocol.

sentences.zh: 內侍梁師成強市百姓墓田，廣其園圃。

translations.literal: Inner Attendant Liang Shicheng forcibly bought commoners' grave land to enlarge his garden.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuch Liang Shicheng forcibly bought commoners' grave plots to expand his garden.

sentences.zh: 汝文言于上，師成諷宰相黜汝文，出守宣州。

translations.literal: Ruwen spoke of this to the Emperor; Shicheng hinted to the chancellor to demote Ruwen, and he went out to guard Xuanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ruwen reported this; Shicheng persuaded the chancellor to demote him, and he was sent to guard Xuanzhou.

sentences.zh: 先是，汝文在密，檜為郡文學，汝文薦其才，故檜引用之。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Ruwen was in Mizhou, Hui was a prefectural literary officer and Ruwen recommended his talent—therefore Hui employed him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier in Mizhou, Hui had been a literary officer and Ruwen had recommended him—hence Hui later favored him.

sentences.zh: 然汝文性剛不為檜屈，對案相詬，至目檜為“濁氣”。

translations.literal: Yet Ruwen's nature was firm and he would not yield to Hui; facing each other at the desk they reviled one another, even calling Hui "murky air."
translations.idiomatic: Yet Ruwen was stubborn and would not bow to Hui; they shouted at each other across the desk, Ruwen even calling Hui "murky air."

sentences.zh: 汝文風度翹楚，好古博雅，精於篆籀，有文集行於世。

translations.literal: Ruwen's bearing was outstanding; he loved antiquity and was broadly learned, skilled in seal script, and had a collected works circulating in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Distinguished in manner, learned in antiquity, skilled in seal script, he left collected works still read today.

sentences.zh: 先是，河東經制使王燮既遁歸，東京留守宗澤承制以庶權陝西制置使。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Hedong Commissioner Wang Xie had already fled back, Tokyo Defender Zong Ze by provisional order made Shu acting Shaanxi Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, after Hedong commissioner Wang Xie fled home, Tokyo defender Zong Ze provisionally made Wang Shu acting Shaanxi commissioner.

sentences.zh: 會宣諭使謝亮入關，庶移書曰：“夏人之患小而緩，金人之患大而迫，秋高必大舉，盍杖節率兵舉義，驅逐渡河，徐圖恢復。

translations.literal: When Imperial Envoy Xie Liang entered the pass, Shu sent a letter saying: "The Xia trouble is small and slow; the Jin trouble is great and pressing—in autumn they will surely strike on a large scale. Why not take staff and lead troops in righteous action, drive them back across the river, and gradually plan recovery?"
translations.idiomatic: When envoy Xie Liang entered the pass, Shu wrote that Xia raids were minor but Jin invasion imminent in autumn—he urged Liang to raise troops, drive the Jin back across the river, and plan recovery.

sentences.zh: ”亮不能從。

translations.literal: Liang could not follow.
translations.idiomatic: Liang would not agree.

sentences.zh: 金人大入，庶調兵自沿河至馮翊，據險以守。
