translations.literal: The Jin entered on a large scale; Shu deployed troops from along the river to Fuping, holding strategic points to defend.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin invaded in force, Shu deployed troops from the river line to Fuping, holding defiles.

sentences.zh: 金人先已乘冰渡河犯晉寧，侵丹州，又渡清水河，破潼關，秦、隴皆震。

translations.literal: The Jin had already crossed the ice to invade Jining, attacked Danzhou, again crossed the Qingshui River, broke through Tong Pass, and Qin and Long were all shaken.
translations.idiomatic: They crossed the ice at Jining, struck Danzhou, crossed the Qingshui, broke Tong Pass, and shook Qin and Long.

sentences.zh: 庶傳檄諸路，會期討賊。

translations.literal: Shu issued proclamations to the various routes, fixing a date to punish the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Shu issued proclamations along the routes to join in punishing the invaders.

sentences.zh: 涇原統制曲端雅不欲屬庶，以未受命辭；

translations.literal: Jingyuan Commander Qu Duan by nature did not wish to belong to Shu and declined on the ground he had not yet received orders;
translations.idiomatic: Jingyuan commander Qu Duan disliked serving under Shu and refused, saying he had no commission;

sentences.zh: 居數日，告身至，又辭。

translations.literal: after several days the commission arrived, and he declined again.
translations.idiomatic: when the commission arrived days later, he refused again.

sentences.zh: 金人知端與庶不協，並兵寇鄜延。

translations.literal: The Jin, knowing Duan and Shu were not in harmony, combined forces to invade Yan-Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Duan and Shu were at odds, the Jin united to attack Yan-Yan.

sentences.zh: 庶在坊州聞之，夜趨鄜延以遏其沖。

translations.literal: Shu was at Fangzhou when he heard this and rushed by night to Yan-Yan to block their thrust.
translations.idiomatic: At Fangzhou Shu heard and rode overnight to Yan-Yan to block them.

sentences.zh: 金人詭道陷丹州，州界鄜、延之間，庶乃自當延安路。

translations.literal: The Jin by a deceptive route took Danzhou; Dan lay between Yan and Yan—Shu then took the Yan'an route upon himself.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin took Danzhou by a ruse; Shu then covered the Yan'an route himself.

sentences.zh: 時端盡統涇原勁兵，庶屢督其進，端訖不行，遂陷延安。

translations.literal: At that time Duan commanded all Jingyuan's crack troops; Shu repeatedly urged him to advance, but Duan in the end would not move, and Yan'an fell.
translations.idiomatic: Duan held Jingyuan's best troops; Shu urged attack repeatedly, but Duan never moved and Yan'an fell.

sentences.zh: 語在端傳。

translations.literal: The account is in Duan's biography.
translations.idiomatic: The account appears in Qu Duan's biography.

sentences.zh: 初，庶聞圍急，自收散亡往援。

translations.literal: At first, when Shu heard the siege was urgent, he gathered scattered troops to go to the rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing the siege was desperate, Shu gathered scattered troops to relieve it.

sentences.zh: 觀察使王燮亦將所部發興元。

translations.literal: Observation Commissioner Wang Xie also led his command from Xingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Observation commissioner Wang Xie also marched from Xingyuan.

sentences.zh: 庶至甘泉而延安已不守，既無所歸，遂以軍付燮，而自將百騎馳至襄樂勞軍，尚倚端為助。

translations.literal: Shu reached Ganquan but Yan'an was already lost; with nowhere to go he handed the army to Xie, while he himself led a hundred horsemen to Xiang-le to encourage the troops, still relying on Duan for help.
translations.idiomatic: Reaching Ganquan he found Yan'an gone; he gave the army to Xie and rode with a hundred men to Xiang-le to rally troops, still counting on Duan.

sentences.zh: 庶至，端令每門減從騎之半，比至帳下，僅數騎。

translations.literal: When Shu arrived, Duan ordered each gate to halve his escort; by the time he reached the tent he had only a few horsemen.
translations.idiomatic: Duan halved his escort at each gate until only a few riders reached the tent.

sentences.zh: 端厲聲問庶延安失守狀，且曰：“節制固知愛身，不知為天子愛城乎？

translations.literal: Duan asked in a harsh voice about the circumstances of Yan'an's fall, and moreover said: "As commissioner you surely know how to spare yourself—do you not know how to spare the Son of Heaven's cities?"
translations.idiomatic: Duan harshly questioned the fall of Yan'an and sneered, "As commissioner you know how to save yourself—do you not save the emperor's cities?"

sentences.zh: ”庶曰：“吾數令不從，誰其愛身者！

translations.literal: Shu said: "I ordered you several times and you would not obey—who is it that spared himself!"
translations.idiomatic: Shu retorted, "I ordered you many times and you disobeyed—who spared himself?"

sentences.zh: ”端怒，謀即軍中誅庶而奪其兵，乃夜走寧州，見謝亮曰：“延安，五路襟喉，今既失矣。

translations.literal: Duan was angry and plotted to execute Shu in the army camp and seize his troops; he fled by night to Ningzhou and saw Xie Liang, saying: "Yan'an is the throat of the Five Routes—now it is lost."
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, Duan plotted to kill Shu in camp and seize his army; he fled by night to Ningzhou and told Xie Liang, "Yan'an was the throat of the Five Routes—and it is lost."

sentences.zh: 《春秋》大夫出疆之義得以專之，請誅庶。

translations.literal: "By the meaning of a great officer leaving his territory in the Spring and Autumn Annals one may act on one's own authority—please execute Shu."
translations.idiomatic: "By the Spring and Autumn rule a minister abroad may act on his own—execute Shu."

sentences.zh: ”亮曰：“使事有指，今以人臣而擅誅於外，是跋扈也，公則自為之。

translations.literal: Liang said: "If the mission had a specific charge, that would be one thing; now for a subject to execute on his own authority outside is overbearing arrogance—you may do it yourself."
translations.idiomatic: Liang replied, "If he had explicit orders that would be different; but for a subject to kill abroad is arrogance—you may do it yourself."

sentences.zh: ”端沮而歸，乃奪庶節制使印，又拘縻其官屬。

translations.literal: Duan was discouraged and returned; he seized Shu's commissioner seal and also detained his staff.
translations.idiomatic: Frustrated, Duan returned, seized Shu's commissioner seal, and detained his staff.

sentences.zh: 會詔庶守京兆，庶先以失律自劾得罷。

translations.literal: An edict then ordered Shu to guard Jingzhao; Shu had already impeached himself for violation of discipline and was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: An edict made Shu guard Jingzhao, but he had already impeached himself for misconduct and resigned.

sentences.zh: 丁內艱。

translations.literal: He observed mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: He mourned his mother.

sentences.zh: 時張浚自富平敗歸，始思庶及端之言可用，乃並召之。

translations.literal: At that time Zhang Jun, returning defeated from Fuping, began to think the words of Shu and Duan could be used; both were summoned.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Jun returned defeated from Fuping he recalled Shu and Duan's counsel and summoned both.

sentences.zh: 庶地近先至，力陳撫秦保蜀之策，勸浚收熙河、秦鳳之兵，扼關、隴以為後圖。

translations.literal: Shu arrived first because he was nearer; he forcefully set forth the policy of pacifying Qin and securing Shu, urging Jun to gather the troops of Xihe, Qin, and Feng and hold the passes and Long as a later plan.
translations.idiomatic: Shu arrived first and urged pacifying Qin and securing Shu, telling Jun to gather Xihe and Qin-Feng troops and hold the passes for a later advance.

sentences.zh: 浚不納。

translations.literal: Jun did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Jun refused.

sentences.zh: 求終制，不許，乃版授參議官。

translations.literal: He begged to complete mourning; this was not allowed; he was appointed by plaque as Deliberation Official.
translations.idiomatic: He begged to finish mourning; denied, he was appointed Deliberation Official by plaque.

sentences.zh: 浚念端與庶必不相容，端未至，但復其官，移恭州。

translations.literal: Jun thought Duan and Shu would surely not get along; Duan had not yet arrived, but only restored his office and moved him to Gongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jun feared Duan and Shu could not coexist; before Duan arrived he restored Shu but moved him to Gongzhou.

sentences.zh: 庶因謂浚曰：“端有反心。

translations.literal: Shu therefore told Jun: "Duan has a rebellious heart."
translations.idiomatic: Shu then told Jun, "Duan harbors rebellion."

sentences.zh: ”浚亦畏端得士，始有殺端意矣。

translations.literal: Jun also feared Duan had won over the troops; he began to intend killing Duan.
translations.idiomatic: Jun also feared Duan's hold on the army and began to contemplate killing him.

sentences.zh: 語在《端傳》。

translations.literal: The account is in the Biography of Duan.
translations.idiomatic: The account is in Qu Duan's biography.

sentences.zh: 紹興五年，起復知興元府、利夔路制置使。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Shaoxing he was raised from mourning to know Xingyuan Prefecture and Commissioner for Li-Kui Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Shaoxing he left mourning to govern Xingyuan and commission Li-Kui.

sentences.zh: 庶以士卒單寡，籍興、洋諸邑及三泉縣強壯，兩丁取一，三丁取二，號“義士”，日閱於縣，月閱於州，厚犒之，不半年，有兵數萬。

translations.literal: Because troops were few, he registered the strong men of Xing, Yang, and the various districts and Sanquan County—one from every two households, two from every three—called "righteous warriors," reviewed daily in the districts and monthly in the prefecture, richly rewarded; within half a year he had tens of thousands of troops.
translations.idiomatic: With few soldiers he enrolled strong men from Xing, Yang, and Sanquan—one per two households or two per three—called "righteous warriors," drilled locally and rewarded; within half a year he had tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 浚言於朝，升徽猷閣直學士。

translations.literal: Jun spoke to court and he was promoted to Direct Academician of the Hall for Cultivating Culture.
translations.idiomatic: Jun reported this and he was promoted to Direct Academician of the Hall for Cultivating Culture.

sentences.zh: 有讒於浚者，徙庶知成都，改嘉州。

translations.literal: Some slandered him to Jun; Shu was moved to know Chengdu and changed to Jiazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Slanderers moved him from Chengdu to Jiazhou.

sentences.zh: 明年，浚劾庶輕率傾險，落職奉祠。

translations.literal: The next year Jun impeached Shu for rashness and dangerous conduct; he lost his post and received a sacrificial stipend.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Jun impeached him for rashness and he lost office with only a stipend.

sentences.zh: 尋起知遂寧，固避得請。

translations.literal: Soon he was raised to know Suining but firmly declined and was granted his request.
translations.idiomatic: Soon offered Suining, he firmly declined and was allowed to rest.

sentences.zh: 六年，除湖北安撫使、知鄂州。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was appointed Pacification Commissioner for Hubei and prefect of Ezhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he became Hubei pacification commissioner and prefect of Ezhou.

sentences.zh: 趨闕，上因燕見，庶言：“陛下欲保江南，無所事；

translations.literal: Hurrying to court, at a banquet audience Shu said: "If Your Majesty wishes only to preserve the south of the Yangzi, there is nothing to do;
translations.idiomatic: At a banquet audience he said, "If Your Majesty only wishes to hold south of the Yangzi, nothing need be done;

sentences.zh: 如曰紹復大業，都荊為可。

translations.literal: "if you say to restore the great enterprise, making Jing the capital would do."
translations.idiomatic: "but to restore the empire, Jing should be the capital."

sentences.zh: 荊州左吳右蜀，利盡南海，前臨江、漢，出三川，涉大河，以圖中原，曹操所以畏關羽者也。

translations.literal: "Jingzhou has Wu on the left and Shu on the right, profits reach the Southern Sea, faces the Jiang and Han in front, exits the Three Gorges, crosses the Great River to plan the Central Plains—this was why Cao Cao feared Guan Yu."
translations.idiomatic: "Jing lies between Wu and Shu, commands the southern sea and the Jiang-Han, opens the Three Gorges and the Great River route to the Central Plains—what made Cao Cao fear Guan Yu."

sentences.zh: ”上大異之。

translations.literal: The Emperor was greatly struck by this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly impressed.

sentences.zh: 復顯謨閣待制、知荊南府、湖北經略安撫使，又復直學士。

translations.literal: Restored as Awaiting Instruction at the Hall for Manifest Instruction, he knew Jingnan Prefecture and was Pacification Commissioner for Hubei, and again restored as Direct Academician.
translations.idiomatic: He was restored as Awaiting Instruction, made prefect of Jingnan and Hubei pacification commissioner, and again Direct Academician.

sentences.zh: 七年十月，以兵部侍郎召。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the seventh year he was summoned as Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the seventh year he was summoned as Vice Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 明年春，入對，上曰：“召卿之日，張浚已去，趙鼎未來，此朕親擢，非有左右之助。

translations.literal: In the spring of the next year he entered for audience; the Emperor said: "On the day I summoned you, Zhang Jun had already left and Zhao Ding had not yet come—this is My personal elevation, not help from favorites."
translations.idiomatic: Next spring at audience the emperor said, "When I called you, Zhang Jun was gone and Zhao Ding not yet arrived—this was my own choice, not a favorite's doing."

sentences.zh: ”庶頓首謝，因奏：“恢復之功十年未立，其失在偏聽，在欲速，在輕爵賞，是非邪正混淆。

translations.literal: Shu bowed his head in thanks and memorialized: "The achievement of restoration has not been established in ten years; its failures lie in partial listening, in haste, in slighting rewards for merit—the distinction of right and wrong and honest and corrupt is confused."
translations.idiomatic: Shu thanked him and said ten years had failed to restore the empire through partial counsel, haste, and careless rewards—right and wrong were blurred.

sentences.zh: 誠能賞功罰罪，其誰不服？

translations.literal: "If one truly rewards merit and punishes guilt, who will not submit?"
translations.idiomatic: "Reward merit and punish guilt, and who will not obey?"

sentences.zh: 昔漢光武以兵取天下，不以不急奪其費，不知兵者不可使言兵。

translations.literal: "Formerly Emperor Guangwu took the realm by arms yet did not seize urgent funds from those who did not know war; one must not make those who do not know war speak of war."
translations.idiomatic: "Guangwu conquered by arms yet did not strip funds from non-soldiers—do not let men ignorant of war dictate war."

sentences.zh: ”又口陳手畫秦、蜀利害。

translations.literal: He also orally stated and traced with his hand the advantages and harms of Qin and Shu.
translations.idiomatic: He also traced Qin and Shu's strategic gains and losses with his hand.

sentences.zh: 上大喜，即日遷本部尚書。

translations.literal: The Emperor was greatly pleased and that same day promoted him to Minister of his department.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted and that day made him Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 閱月，拜樞密副使。

translations.literal: Within a month he was appointed Vice Commissioner of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Within a month he became Vice Commissioner of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 議者乞遣重臣行邊，遂命庶措置江、淮邊防。

translations.literal: Debaters begged dispatch of a heavy minister to tour the frontier; Shu was therefore ordered to arrange Jiang-Huai border defense.
translations.idiomatic: When the court sought a senior minister to tour the frontier, Shu was ordered to arrange Jiang-Huai defenses.

sentences.zh: 京、湖宣撫使岳飛聞庶行邊，遺書曰：“今歲若不出師，當納節請閑。

translations.literal: Jing-Hu Pacification Commissioner Yue Fei, hearing Shu was touring the frontier, sent a letter saying: "If we do not campaign this year, I will surrender my seal and request leisure."
translations.idiomatic: Yue Fei, pacification commissioner of Jing-Hu, wrote that if no campaign came that year he would surrender his command and retire.

sentences.zh: ”庶壯之。

translations.literal: Shu was heartened by this.
translations.idiomatic: Shu was heartened.

sentences.zh: 庶還朝，論金人變詐，自渝海上之盟，因及飛納節之語。

translations.literal: When Shu returned to court he discussed the Jin's deceitful shifts since violating the sea treaty, and also mentioned Fei's words about surrendering his seal.
translations.idiomatic: Back at court he denounced Jin treachery since breaking the sea treaty and cited Fei's threat to resign his command.

sentences.zh: 當是時，秦檜再相，以和戎為事。

translations.literal: At that time Qin Hui was chancellor again and made appeasement his business.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Hui was again chancellor and pursued appeasement.

sentences.zh: 金使烏陵思謀至，詔趣庶還。

translations.literal: The Jin envoy Wulingsimou arrived; an edict hurried Shu back.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin envoy Wulingsimou arrived, an edict recalled Shu.

sentences.zh: 庶力詆和議，乞誅金使，其言甚切。

translations.literal: Shu forcefully denounced the peace talks and begged execution of the Jin envoy; his words were very cutting.
translations.idiomatic: Shu fiercely opposed peace and begged the envoy's execution in the strongest terms.

sentences.zh: 金又遣張通古來許割地，還梓宮，歸太后。

translations.literal: The Jin again sent Zhang Tonggu to offer ceded territory, return the imperial coffins, and restore the empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: Jin sent Zhang Tonggu promising land, imperial coffins, and the empress dowager's return.

sentences.zh: 庶曰：“和議之事，臣所不知。

translations.literal: Shu said: "Matters of peace—I do not know them."
translations.idiomatic: Shu said, "Peace negotiations are not my affair."

sentences.zh: ”凡七疏乞免官，乃以資政殿學士知潭州。

translations.literal: Altogether he submitted seven memorials begging to be removed from office; he was then made Academician of the Hall for Governance and prefect of Tanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized seven times to resign and was made Academician of the Hall for Governance and prefect of Tanzhou.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞勾龍如淵劾庶本趙鼎所薦，欺君罔上。

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Gou Longruyuan impeached Shu as originally recommended by Zhao Ding, deceiving the ruler and misleading the state.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-Chief Gou Longruyuan impeached him as Zhao Ding's protégé who had deceived the throne.

sentences.zh: 庶罷歸，至九江，被命奪職，徙家居焉。

translations.literal: Shu was dismissed and returned; reaching Jiujiang he was ordered stripped of office and made to live at home.
translations.idiomatic: Dismissed on his way home, at Jiujiang he was stripped of rank and confined to his house.

sentences.zh: 十三年，御史胡汝明論庶譏訕朝政，責響德軍節度副使，道州安置。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year Censor Hu Ruming accused Shu of mocking court policy; he was demoted to Military Affairs Vice Commissioner of Xiangde Army and settled in Daozhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year Censor Hu Ruming charged him with ridiculing policy; he was demoted and exiled to Daozhou.

sentences.zh: 至貶所卒。

translations.literal: He died at the place of exile.
translations.idiomatic: He died in exile.

sentences.zh: 孝宗思庶言，追復其官，諡敏節。

translations.literal: Xiaozong recalled Shu's words and posthumously restored his office, posthumous title Minjie.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozong remembered his counsel, restored his rank posthumously, and gave the posthumous title Minjie.

sentences.zh: 子六人，之奇，乾道中，知樞密院事。

translations.literal: He had six sons; Zhiqi, in the Qiandao era, became Commissioner of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He had six sons; Zhiqi became Commissioner of Military Affairs in the Qiandao era.

sentences.zh: 辛炳，字如晦，福州候官縣人。

translations.literal: Xin Bing, courtesy name Ruhui, was a native of Houguan County in Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xin Bing, whose courtesy name was Ruhui, came from Houguan in Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 登元符三年進士第，累官至監察御史兼權殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi in the third year of Yuanfu and rose through offices to Investigating Censor with acting appointment as Palace Attendant Censor within the Hall.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi in the third year of Yuanfu and rose to Investigating Censor with acting Palace Attendant Censor.

sentences.zh: 先是，蔡京廢發運司轉般倉為直達綱，舟入，率侵盜，沉舟而遁，戶部受虛數，人畏京莫敢言。

translations.literal: Earlier, Cai Jing abolished the Transport Commission's transit granaries for direct convoys; when boats entered they mostly plundered, sank the boats and fled, the Ministry of Revenue received fictitious numbers, and people feared Jing and dared not speak.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Cai Jing replaced transport granaries with direct convoys; crews often looted, scuttled boats, and fled, leaving the Ministry of Revenue false receipts—none dared speak for fear of Jing.

sentences.zh: 炳極疏其弊，且以變法後兩歲所得之數，較常歲虧欠一百三十有二萬，支益廣而入寢微，乞下有司計度。

translations.literal: Bing memorialized vehemently on their abuses and moreover compared receipts for the two years after the reform with normal years—a deficit of 1.32 million—and expenditures growing wider while income grew thinner; he begged the relevant offices to calculate.
translations.idiomatic: Bing denounced the abuses, showing 1.32 million less revenue in two years under the reform, and begged a full accounting.

sentences.zh: 徽宗以問京，京怒，以炳為沮撓，責監南劍州新豐場，尋提舉洞霄宮，起知袁州，移無為軍。

translations.literal: Huizong asked Jing; Jing was angry that Bing was obstructing and punished him as supervisor of the Xinfeng field in Nanjian; soon he was made custodian of the Dongxiao Palace, raised to know Yuanzhou, and moved to Wuwei Army.
translations.idiomatic: Huizong asked Jing, who punished Bing as obstructive, posting him to Nanjian; later he became Dongxiao custodian, then prefect of Yuan and Wuwei.

sentences.zh: 靖康初，召為兵部員外郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingkang he was summoned as Secretary in the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: At Jingkang's start he was summoned as Secretary in the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 高宗即位，除左司員外郎，辭；

translations.literal: When Gaozong took the throne he was appointed Left Department Secretary; he declined;
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozong ascended he was made Left Department Secretary but declined;

sentences.zh: 未幾，起直龍圖閣、知潭州。

translations.literal: before long he was raised as Direct Palace with dragon-designation and prefect of Tanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: soon he was raised as Direct Palace and prefect of Tanzhou.

sentences.zh: 明年，張浚調兵潭州，以炳懦怯不能，罷之，尋以起居舍人召，辭。

translations.literal: The next year Zhang Jun mobilized troops in Tanzhou; because Bing was cowardly and incapable he was dismissed; soon summoned as Attendant of the Secretariat, he declined.
translations.idiomatic: Next year Zhang Jun mobilized in Tanzhou and removed him as incompetent; summoned as Secretariat Attendant, he again declined.

sentences.zh: 紹興二年，復以侍御史召。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shaoxing he was again summoned as Attendant Censor.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Shaoxing he was again summoned as Attendant Censor.

sentences.zh: 首言今日公道壅塞，風俗頹薄，連疏三省所行乖失數十事，請諭大臣勿廢都堂公見之禮。

translations.literal: He first said that today the public way is blocked and custom decadent; in successive memorials he listed several tens of matters in which the three departments acted wrongly and begged the great ministers not to abandon the shared deliberation of the chief hall.
translations.idiomatic: He opened by saying public justice was choked and morals decayed, then listed dozens of errors by the three departments and urged ministers to preserve open deliberation.

sentences.zh: 時福建八州添差至百八十餘員，炳言：“艱危多事之時，冗食之官無益，當罷。

translations.literal: At that time the eight prefectures of Fujian had more than 180 supernumerary appointees; Bing said: "In a time of hardship and many affairs, idle eating officials are useless—they should be abolished."
translations.idiomatic: Fujian's eight prefectures held over 180 supernumerary posts; Bing said in hard times such posts should be cut.

sentences.zh: ”從之。

translations.literal: The Emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 蘇、湖地震，下詔求言。

translations.literal: Su and Hu had earthquakes; an edict sought opinions.
translations.idiomatic: Earthquakes struck Su and Hu; the court sought opinions.

sentences.zh: 炳言：“大臣無畏天之心，何事不可為？

translations.literal: Bing said: "Great ministers lack a heart that fears Heaven—what affair can they not do?"
translations.idiomatic: Bing said, "Ministers who do not fear Heaven will dare anything."

sentences.zh: ”其言甚峻，由是宰執呂頤浩居家待罪，炳劾罷頤浩。

translations.literal: His words were very stern; because of this Chancellor Lü Yihao remained at home awaiting punishment; Bing impeached and removed Yihao.
translations.idiomatic: His tone was severe; Lü Yihao awaited punishment at home and Bing impeached him out of office.

sentences.zh: 知樞密院事張浚召赴行在，炳論其敗事誤國，浚坐落職。

translations.literal: Military Affairs Commissioner Zhang Jun was summoned to the traveling palace; Bing argued he had failed in affairs and harmed the state; Jun lost his post.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Jun was recalled, Bing charged him with failure and harm to the state, and Jun was removed.

sentences.zh: 除御史中丞。

translations.literal: He was appointed Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 時方遣使議和，炳方言：“金人無信，和議不可恃，宜講求守禦攻戰之策。

translations.literal: At that time envoys were being sent to discuss peace; Bing just then said: "The Jin are faithless—peace talks cannot be relied upon; one ought to seek policies of defense, preparation, attack, and war."
translations.idiomatic: As peace envoys were dispatched, Bing warned that the Jin were faithless and the court must prepare defense and war.

sentences.zh: ”以疾請外，除顯謨閣直學士、知漳州，未赴而卒。

translations.literal: Citing illness he begged an outside post; he was appointed Direct Academician of the Hall for Manifest Instruction and prefect of Zhangzhou; before he went he died.
translations.idiomatic: Ill, he sought an outside post as Direct Academician and prefect of Zhangzhou but died before taking it.

sentences.zh: 詔：炳任中執法，操行清修，今其雲亡，貧無以葬，賜銀帛賻其家，贈通議大夫。

translations.literal: An edict said: Bing in office upheld the law, his conduct pure and cultivated; now that he has passed among the clouds, he is too poor to bury—grant silver and silk to assist his family; posthumously grant Grand Master for Governance.
translations.idiomatic: An edict praised his upright service and poverty at death, granted funeral silver, and posthumously made him Grand Master for Governance.

sentences.zh: 論曰：秦檜晚薦士以收人望，然一時知名之士，亦豈盡可籠絡者哉！

translations.literal: The Commentary says: In his later years Hui recommended scholars to win public esteem—yet could all famous men of the time really be drawn in?
translations.idiomatic: The Commentary says: Qin Hui late in life promoted scholars for prestige—yet not every famous man could be co-opted.

sentences.zh: 朱倬論事輒不合，王綸代言辭合體要，若尹穡、王之望人品雖不同，其附和議則一爾。

translations.literal: Zhu Zhuo whenever he spoke on affairs ran counter to policy; Wang Lun's drafted words fit the essentials; though Yin Se and Wang Zhiwang differed in character, in joining the peace faction they were one.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Zhuo clashed with policy whenever he spoke; Wang Lun's drafts were apt; Yin Se and Wang Zhiwang differed in character yet alike backed peace.

sentences.zh: 徐俯末與赴鼎爭辨，沮抑岳飛，異哉。

translations.literal: Xu Fu in the end disputed with Zhao Ding and obstructed Yue Fei—how strange.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Fu finally fought Zhao Ding and blocked Yue Fei—an odd case.

sentences.zh: 沈與求止和親之議，翟汝文善料事，而檜以為異己。

translations.literal: Shen Yuqiu stopped the peace talks; Di Ruwen was good at foreseeing events, yet Hui treated him as a personal enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Yuqiu opposed peace; Di Ruwen foresaw well, yet Hui counted him an enemy.

sentences.zh: 王庶論都荊州，當時諸臣之慮皆不及此。

translations.literal: Wang Shu argued for making Jingzhou the capital—at the time no other minister's thought reached this.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shu urged Jing as capital—a vision other ministers lacked.

sentences.zh: 考夫祈寬之事，庶蓋忠義人也。

translations.literal: Considering the matter of praying for leniency, Shu was surely a man of loyalty and righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: In the matter of pleading for mercy, Shu was plainly loyal and righteous.

sentences.zh: 辛炳雅志清修，又豈多見也歟。

translations.literal: Xin Bing's constant aim was pure cultivation—how seldom is such a man seen!
translations.idiomatic: Xin Bing's lifelong aim was integrity—how rare such men are!
